After a second straight loss in ACC play, Louisville looks to get back on track when it hosts Florida State at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium in Louisville, Ky., on Friday at 7 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Cardinals are 4.5-point home favorites, but my Florida State vs. Louisville prediction and college football picks expect the Seminoles' offense to take advantage of one of the country's worst defenses. Who will win Florida State vs Louisville: Florida State +4.5 Florida State is coming off a narrative-changing victory after beating Virginia by 31 points. The Seminoles have now covered in each of their last two games against FBS opponents, showcasing one of the country's best run games. With Ashton Daniels at QB and Ousmane Kromah at running back, FSU is 12th nationally in EPA per rush and 17th in rush success rate (49.7%). That could be a problem for a Louisville defense that's been one of the worst in the Power Four, allowing the 14th-most yards per game in the country (423). Daniels and Kromah have combined for 755 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns in five games, and if they get going on the ground, Florida State can turn this into a shootout on the road. I like FSU at +3.5 or better . TOP PICK Florida State vs Louisville Over/Under pick: Over 59.5 Louisville has an offense that looks capable of winning the ACC and a defense that looks capable of losing every game against a quality opponent. In four FBS games, Louisville has averaged 33.5 points per game and allowed 33.2 ppg. The Cardinals have hit the Over in three of those games, and I like them to do it again with a total of 60.5 or better . With Lincoln Kienholz expected to be healthy for Louisville, he should keep the offense humming. The Cardinals rank top 25 nationally in offensive success rate (49.7%) , and Kienholz has accounted for 15 touchdowns and a 77.2 QBR. Kienholz, along with running back Isaac Brown (and Keyjuan Brown if he plays), should push a Florida State defense that's 98th in rush success rate (46.9%) and 93rd in net adjusted EPA per play. Florida State vs Louisville combo Louisville's defense is the reason it's already lost three games this season and why it's failed to cover in two straight ACC matchups. Louisville doesn't create negative plays on defense, ranking third-last in the ACC in havoc rate (13.2%) and 88th in net EPA per play. With Kromah and Daniels carrying FSU's ground attack, they will be able to break loose for big plays and approach 30+ points. Meanwhile, FSU has defensive issues of its own, ranking 92nd in available yards percentage (52.1%) . A high-scoring game should lead to a back-and-forth final frame. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:58 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's amazing how fast two weeks can change things. Louisville appeared to be ready to make a charge with a close loss to Ole Miss, a great 41-31 win over SMU, and winnable games coming up. A 30-27 loss to Wake Forest and a 31-28 loss to NC State later, and now the Cardinals have to win to stay alive in the ACC race. Florida State was done. Head coach Mike Norvell was all but fired, and then everything flipped. The Seminoles tuned up against Central Arkansas, and then stunned Virginia 38-7. Win this, and the season narrative totally changes. Florida State vs Louisville Quick Hits Florida State is on the road for four games in the next five, with a trip to Miami up next before hosting Clemson. Louisville goes to Syracuse next to start a run of three road games in four dates. Before the last meeting in the 2023 ACC Championship, the two teams split the previous ten games. How To Watch Florida State vs Louisville Date: Friday, October 9, 2026 Game Time: 7:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville, KY – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why Florida State Will Win So what did Florida State do against Virginia to generate all of this excitement? The defense pitched one of its best games in a long time, considering the circumstances, holding the Cavalier passing game in check with a monstrous day from the pass rush. The Noles generated ten sacks and 12 tackles for loss. The relentless pressure should continue against a Louisville offensive front that's having a problem keeping teams out of the backfield. Why Louisville Will Win Can Florida State show up on the road? It's not quite fair to dog the Noles for losing at Alabama, but the program has lost 13 straight games outside of Tallahassee, going back to the win over Florida late in 2023. Louisville has to take a deep breath after the NC State loss. It played well. The ground game was great, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz was fine on his dinged up ankle, and everything was fine outside of three lost fumbles. Florida State hasn't forced a takeaway in a month. Florida State vs Louisville Prediction, Betting Lines Florida State isn't awful. The pieces are there – the ground game is solid, and look out if that pass rush keeps on rolling – but they have a hard time always fitting together. The Seminoles will crank up plenty of yards and points – the Louisville defense isn't anything special – but the offense will stall a few too many times, and the Cardinals will find their offensive scoring punch after two straight disappointments. Louisville 38, Florida State 30 Latest Consensus Line: Louisville -3.5, o/u: 59.5 ATS Confidence (out of 5) : 4 Must See Rating (out of 5) : 3.5 Consensus line based on BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, and FanDuel. picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Louisville Cardinals | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 8, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football Can FSU win their third straight against Louisville to go 4-2 on the season? The Florida State Seminoles are traveling to Kentucky to meet the Louisville Cardinals for another ACC Friday Night Lights game at the L&N Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. and will be televised on ESPN. Florida State (3-2, 1-1 ACC) leads the all-time series 18-6, including a 7-3 record at Louisville (2-3, 1-2 ACC). FSU has won the last two games against the Cardinals, including a 16-6 victory in the 2023 ACC Championship Game and a 35-31 win in their most recent regular-season matchup in Louisville in 2022. The Cardinals are 4-6 against the Seminoles since joining the ACC in 2014. The Cardinals took a second straight defeat last Saturday, dropping a 31-28 contest at NC State. All three of Louisville’s losses this season have come by three points. Seven of its last eight losses dating back to 2024 have come by three points or less. The Cardinals have eight touchdowns of 50 yards or more this season, the most of any team in FBS. Five different Louisville players have scored a touchdown of 50 yards or more this season. Louisville is averaging 486 yards per game, second-best in the ACC, and has 37 plays of 20 yards or more through five games, tied with Indiana for the most in the country. Quarterback Lincoln Kienholz has rushed for 158 yards on the ground this season and is tied for fifth nationally among quarterbacks with six rushing touchdowns. In the first five games, Kienholz has completed 96 of 139 of his passes for a 69.1 completion percentage, 9 touchdowns with 1 interception, and is averaging 278 yards per game. The Cardinals rushed for 231 yards in the loss at NC State, with Miami native Isaac Brown rushing for 125 yards on nine carries, his 12th 100-yard game. Keyjuan Brown leads the Cardinals in rushing with 367 yards, averaging 9.7 yards per carry. Wide receiver Tre Richardson leads the Cards with 28 receptions for 445 receiving yards and has scored three touchdowns (2 receiving, 1 rushing). The three touchdowns Richardson has scored this season have been 30, 62, and 38 yards. Of his 33 offensive touches this season, 19 have gone for at least 10 yards and nine have covered 20 yards or more. The only player in the ACC with more plays of 20 yards or more is Miami’s Malachi Toney. Tight end Jaleel Skinner has hauled in 14 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns through five games. Skinner is one of just 20 players in the FBS to have multiple 60-yard plays from scrimmage and the only tight end to do it, scoring touchdowns from 61 and 69 yards. Overall, the Cardinals rank 17th in the nation in total offense (486 yards/game), 22nd in scoring offense (38.6 points/game), T-24th in passing offense (287.4 yards/game), and 38th in rushing offense (198.6 yards/game). Similar to the Seminoles, Louisville’s defense is struggling. Linebacker J.T. Capers leads the defense with 38 tackles, followed by defensive back Kaleb Beasley with 35 tackles and 3 interceptions. The Cardinal defense ranks 125th in total defense, giving up 423 yards per game, 130th in passing yards allowed (267 yards/game), and 113th in scoring defense (29.2 points/game). Florida State is coming off its most impressive win of the season, notching a 38-7 win over Virginia last Saturday. Quarterback Ashton Daniels’ five touchdowns in the victory set an FSU record, now placing him third nationally with nine rushing touchdowns and ranked 3rd with 15.87 yards per completion, while also leading the ACC in rushing scores and in yards per completion. His 183 passing yards, career-high 136 rushing yards, and five touchdowns against Virginia make him the only FBS player since 1995 to reach those marks in a game. FSU 38, Virginia 7: Seminoles dominate Cavaliers in all three phases in blowout win FSU’s improving defense now ranks 103rd in the nation, giving up 385 yards/game, 127th in passing defense (266 yards/game), and ranked T-98th in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert almost 41% of the time on third-down attempts. However, the Noles’ defense has been decent at stopping opponents behind the line of scrimmage, averaging 3.4 sacks per game for 8th best in the nation, and 20th in tackles for loss with 7.2 TFLs per game. Louisville junior wide receiver Lawayne McCoy played two seasons at Florida State before transferring this year to Louisville. In two years with the Seminoles, McCoy played in 20 games with 33 receptions for 448 yards and three touchdowns. Florida State Director of Football Strategy/Offensive Assistant Gabe Fertitta was a quality control assistant at Louisville during the 2021 season. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Louisville Cardinals Florida State is trending as a 3.5-point underdog, with the over/under set at 59.5 points according to FanDuel. Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Curt Weiler (season record: 4-1, 2-3 ATS) Welp. Last week’s game is certainly making me at least consider the possibility that I was being a bit harsh about this team. Somehow, FSU enters this game with a better record than Louisville. The Seminoles haven’t won a road game since 2023, but this Louisville team is coming off back-to-back losses to Wake Forest and NC State and has a knack for making a lot of mistakes. I’m still not convinced that FSU has turned over a new leaf, but as a show of faith, I’ll give them some benefit of the doubt. Florida State 31, Louisville 27 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-1 ) FSU took down a genuinely good team in Virginia, and looking back on the Alabama game, we were probably the best punch against them up to this point that ended up losing. I’m going to go out on a pretty rickety limb here and say that FSU finally ends its 1,000+ day road losing streak and defeats Louisville. Louisville’s run defense is allowing 156.2 rushing yards per game, ranking 92nd nationally. If Wisner and company can establish the run, or if Daniels can go for five touchdowns again, it’ll be a fun time for the Seminoles. Give me FSU to pull off the “upset.” FSU 41, Louisville 31 NoleThruandThru (season record: 5-0) Louisville 41, FSU 38 Jessi Wynn (season record: 3-0) Florida State enters the matchup with momentum from a two-game winning streak, including a dominant 38-7 win over Virginia. The Seminoles looked strong on both sides of the ball, with the offense finding success in both the running and passing games. FSU has struggled on the road, but I think the confidence from this winning streak will carry over. Noles 39, Louisville 32 Jordan Silversmith (season record: 4-1) Like everyone else, I have to reconsider how I think the next three games will go for Florida State after last week’s win against Virginia. The Seminoles ripped through the UVA offensive line for 10 sacks, ran the quarterback effectively, and played their cleanest game in what seems like forever. They also get a break, even though they travel on a short week, by facing a reeling Louisville team that has lost two in a row. Plus, for whatever reason, FSU has played well against the Cards the last few times they have met. However, one win isn’t enough for me to trust this team, especially on the road. The defense will have its hands full against Jeff Brohm’s offense, and one week does not mean all the problems are solved. FSU keeps this game close, but a bad turnover and a back-breaking touchdown drive result in a loss. Take UL to cover and the over. UL 34, FSU 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 4-0) I need to see it to believe it when it comes to FSU on the road; Louisville’s pass rush is fierce, so a successful formula is a lot of QB power and play-action shot. Louisville is bloodied and a mess on defense, but FSU hasn’t won a road game since 2023, so…. Louisville 35 , FSU 31 Jon Marchant (season record: 4-1 ) Louisville looked like a good, solid squad, but they keep losing close games. FSU, meanwhile, looked like a completely different team from what we’ve seen since 2023. Will the real FSU please stand up? Can FSU win this game? Yes. But Friday night on the road is tough. Louisville 28 , FSU 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 4-1) Friday’s game might be a battle of which team has the ball last. There should be a decent amount of points scored on both sides, though FSU could always “struggle.” In the end, I think UL has more firepower, and old friend Lawayne McCoy makes some key plays to secure the Louisville win. Louisville 45, FSU 38 Matt Minnick (season record: 4-1, 4-1 ATS) My, how the tables turn. All of a sudden, Louisville is the team in disarray, while Florida State is coming off its best game since beating Alabama to open the 2025 season. FSU’s offense has looked very good for large stretches the last few weeks, and most of those stretches occur when Norvell simplifies the number of reads Ashton Daniels has to process. If that continues, the ‘Noles should have no problem scoring 24+ points, as they have in every game this season. Will 24 be enough? Not likely. Even in back-to-back losses, UL has put up 27 and 28 points, respectively. I need to see more than one week of good defense to believe FSU will hold UL to a season low on a short week in Louisville. So now the question becomes: can Florida State outscore the Cardinals? Call me crazy, but I say yes! FSU 34, Louisville 30 Frank DaNole (season record: 3-2) These two teams are similar in that both have decent offenses while fielding defenses that leave a lot to be desired. This will be the second game when everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are only 3.5-point underdogs as the road team for a reason. Vegas knows it, and the Seminoles know it. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed last week. The Seminoles may not dominate at all three positional units for the entire game, but in the end FSU will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their equally talented Cardinal opponents. FSU Seminoles 38, Louie’s Flock 31 Perry Kostidakis (season record: 3-2, 3-2 ATS) If there was ever a time for FSU to continue its success with its front seven, it’s this game. The Cardinals’ offensive line has struggled this season, giving up two sacks (81st in the country) and 6.4 tackles for loss (121st) per game. Defensively, Louisville has struggled as much as Florida State has — its 266.8 passing yards per game allowed ranks 130th in the country (FSU is 127 with 265.6) — so even if the defensive turnaround on the Seminoles’ end was fugazi, I do have confidence in their ability to put up points after another successful offensive showing. What are the things that give me pause? away.headline: Updated week 5 injury report adds to a growing issue within Florida State's defense
away.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. The Seminoles will be without four linebackers after the LaVallee announcement, as the freshman will join Izayia Williams, Blake Nichelson, and Daylen Green on the sidelines this week. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. Florida State and Virginia both released lengthy injury reports ahead of the Week 5 battle on Saturday. Both teams will be without a good chunk of the roster, but the key difference is that the Seminoles will be without multiple players at a vital position, and another player from the same position just joined that list. 2026 has not been the most productive season up to this point for Florida State, with a handful of players powering through bumps and bruises to compensate for the number of more serious injuries, particularly on defense. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. Cottrill, on the other hand, saw action against SMU and Central Arkansas, totaling two tackles. During the Week 3 game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa, Florida State only played four linebackers and opted to use plenty of defensive backs. With Mikai Gbayor, Chris Jones, and Omar Graham Jr. all expected to play in Week 5, the Seminoles' staff might just give the remaining snaps at linebacker to the more experienced Cottrill. The only issue, however, is that Alabama and Virginia are far different teams in terms of how the offense attacks opposing defenses. Virginia is going to look to keep the football on the ground for most of the game. When combined with the play-action heavy passing attack, the Seminoles' linebackers could tire easily, which will force more of the remaining depth into the game. The updated injury report delivered a few positive bits of news for Florida State, as Ashlynd Barker, Chris Jones, KJ Kirkland, Donny Hiebert, and Xavier Tiller were all upgraded

picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. There's still plenty of work to do after this week, but beating the defending national champion – and putting an end to Indiana's 21-game winning streak – would be just the moment the program has been waiting for to show that it's headed in the right direction. Indiana hasn't been the dominant version of last year, but it's still unbeaten, it's about as tuned up as it can be, and it got its first road game out of the way with a 47-15 win over Rutgers. Yeah, this might be Nebraska's moment. It's also Curt Cignetti's moment to prove that for the Hoosiers, it's business as usual. Indiana vs Nebraska Quick Hits The Hoosiers get three home games in the next four after this, but Ohio State is up next, the road date is at Michigan, and then Minnesota and USC come to Bloomington. Nebraska goes on the road for three games in the next four dates, with a trip to Oregon before a week off to get ready for Washington. Indiana won 56-7 in 2024, but the Huskers are 6-1 in the series before that going back to a Hoosier win in 1959. It has only turned the ball over once, it's third in the nation in fewest penalties, and no one does a better job of not putting itself in tough situations. It might not be that Nebraska needs to force mistakes and can win this straight up, but it has a way of pulling away in games, helped by the takeaways. On the flip side, the Huskers were flagged 16 times in the win over Maryland and have committed the most penalties of any Big Ten team so far. Why Nebraska Will Win The Hoosiers have only been stress-tested once in the 29-23 win over Northwestern, and that was partly because Wildcat quarterback Aidan Chiles was accurate with the passing game. Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea might not be Drew Brees, but he's hitting 66% of his passes with 13 touchdowns and just two picks. This has to be about the Nebraska offensive line, though. The Huskers are taking over games with the running game pushing until the dam breaks, and then games turn into routs. Indiana isn't Maryland or Bowling Green, but Michigan State is a tough-as-nails team that was the only team that held the Huskers to under 200 yards, and it still lost by 18. Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction, Betting Lines Can Nebraska get close to 40 carries? Part of the problem against Indiana is that teams have to give up on the run because it doesn't work. Only North Texas has been able to get past 66 yards this season, and it's also the only team that ran more than 35 times. North Texas also lost 52-16. The energy of the moment will carry the Huskers to a solid first half, but they won't be able to pull away. Eventually, the Nebraska run defense will start to buckle, the IU pass rush will get to Colandrea, and the hype for the Ohio State game will start about 30 seconds after the final gun. away.headline: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers
away.blurb: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers Skip to main content SI.COM Indiana could be without its leading rusher Saturday night when the Hoosiers take on Rutgers, with running back Lee Beebe Jr. listed as a game-time decision, per the Big Ten's availability report . Beebe, who rushed for 203 yards in Indiana's win over Northwestern last week, was a midweek addition to the availability report. His status headlines an otherwise encouraging final injury update for the Hoosiers, who had three players removed from the report ahead of their first road test of the season. Richard was listed as probable Friday before being removed from Saturday's report, putting him in line to handle the bulk of Indiana's rushing workload should Beebe be unable to go. Cuono, a second-year depth running back with 11 carries for 45 yards this season, would likely serve as Richard's primary backup in that scenario. True freshman Jayreon Campbell, who has rushed six times for 43 yards in limited action, is also available. Khobie Martin, meanwhile, remains out for the fourth consecutive game as he continues recovering from a forearm injury he suffered in Indiana's season opener against North Texas. Martin is expected to return around the midway point of the season. Indiana enters Saturday with a rushing attack ranked among the nation's top 10, although Beebe's potential absence would leave the Hoosiers without one of their most productive offensive weapons. Linebacker Rolijah Hardy, who was listed as probable Friday after suffering an injury late in his eight-tackle performance against Northwestern, was also removed from Saturday's availability report and is expected to play. A.J. Harris, Daniel Ndukwe among those ruled out Defensive end Daniel Ndukwe is also out, marking his first absence of the season. Ndukwe ranks second on the team with 4.5 tackles for loss, including 1.5 against Northwestern last week. Indiana still has considerable depth at edge, with Stephen Daley, Kellan Wyatt, Tobi Osunsanmi, Chiddi Obiazor and Josh Burnham available to help absorb his absence. Elsewhere, cornerback Carson Williams and wide receiver Lebron Bond remain out for the third and fourth consecutive games, respectively. Indiana and Rutgers are scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET. home.blurb: Sitting at 0-6 on the year, the Eagles put out a statement on X saying that they were canceling the rest of the season due to injuries. The Eagles only played four games on the field and had forfeited two due to injury concerns. Their remaining games included a road trip to Blue Hill (NE), a home against Southern Valley (NE) on Oct. 16 and they were set to close out the year on the road at Pleasanton (NE) on Oct. 23. For the Overton (NE) Eagles, the 2026 high school football season has been a year to forget. After six games, they can officially put 2026 behind them. In the games they played, Overton had been outscored 209-34. Last week they lost to Axtell (NE) 38-6. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. "Due to recent injuries, Overton High School has made the difficult decision to forfeit the remaining football games of the 2026 season," the statement from the school reads. :We would like to thank our players and coaches for their dedication, effort, and commitment throughout the season. We appreciate their determination to compete and play as many games as possible despite the challenges faced. "We apologize to our remaining opponents for any inconvenience this decision may cause and appreciate their understanding. We also thank our families, fans, and community for their continued support of Overton Eagle Football." With the season now officially over, the Eagles have their first losing season since 2023. That year they finished 4-5 and before that went 1-7. They'll look to bounce back from this current run of bad results like they did during the 2022 and 2023 stretch. Arizona (4-1, 1-1 in Big 12) now heads out to the country roads of West Virginia, where they will face a high-scoring Mountaineers squad in the midst of a two-game losing streak. West Virginia bullied then No. 25 Virginia, 38-27, in Week 3 to build momentum heading into Big 12 play. Things haven't gone well for coach Rich Rodriguez's team since then, however, with an ugly 41-24 home loss to Oklahoma State followed by a shootout at Iowa State that ended in a 45-42 defeat after Cyclones running back Aiden Flora scored his fifth touchdown with 1:57 left in the fourth quarter. Now they'll level up against the best rushing attack in the country. WVU has 1,470 rushing yards on the season, which not only leads the FBS but is 133 yards more than second place, Army, and 190 yards more than the next high major team in South Carolina. West Virginia's 294 rushing yards per game is third in the FBS, and its 17 rushing touchdowns is tied for third. A big part of the ground attack for the Mountaineers is the dual-threat ability of quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr., who has a whopping 574 rushing yards and 11(!) rushing touchdowns on the season - which is tied with Florida running back Jadan Baugh for the most in the country. picks.headline: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona game, makes a score prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Buccaneers-Cowboys updates Guardians-White Sox updates A'ja Wilson MVP — again NFL Week 5 NFL picks vs. spread Caitlin Clark on Fever future AMES, IA - OCTOBER 3: Head coach Rich Rodriguez of the West Virginia Mountaineers shakes hands with quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. #3 of the West Virginia Mountaineers celebrating a Mountaineers touchdown in the first half of play against the Iowa State Cyclones at Jack Trice Stadium on October 3, 2026, in Ames, Iowa. (Photo by David Purdy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brian Pedersen Tue, October 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's not just Game Week, it's RichRod Game Week! Arizona's first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod's squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: "There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don't think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn't looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering." It's to no one's surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What's been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona's defense will try to neutralize this? "We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn't realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn't what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games." Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? "I think it's fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don't blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage." The Mountaineers' defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? "In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can't get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It's rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley's reputation as a sort of 'mad scientist' on defense could be part of the problem. It's really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn't matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here." How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? "After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I've seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod's first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it's humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn't want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around." Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. "We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. In other words, we have you right where we want you. 45-31 Mountaineers get back on track at home."

Oct 3, 2026 Updated Oct 3, 2026 AMES — Cody Jackson transferred to Iowa State last winter in search of his fourth fresh start. The talented transfer wide receiver found it, but catches proved tough to come by. Until Saturday, when the former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. “I trusted in God, number one, and trusted in my coaches (and) my teammates,” said Jackson, who didn’t record a catch in ISU’s first two games, but now has 12 receptions in the past two games. “Not having my head down. Keeping my head high. Keeping a smile on my face every day and coming in and working at practice.” Jackson’s first grab on Saturday for the Cyclones (3-2, 1-1 Big 12) turned into a 46-yard touchdown on a halfback toss from Aiden Flora. His other seven receptions against the Mountaineers (3-3, 0-2) came during a tense second half, and many fueled three straight scoring drives that helped ISU preserve the win. “He did a great job finding open windows and attacking the ball in the air,” Cyclones quarterback Jaylen Raynor said. Jackson notched 92 yards after the catch and often adjusted his routes as Raynor improvised amid amped up West Virginia pressure. His 43-yard catch on third-and-six early in the fourth quarter set up Kyle Konrardy’s 35-yard field goal that gave ISU a 31-28 lead. And Jackson’s 15-yard grab on the Cyclones’ final scoring drive ended in one of Flora’s three rushing touchdowns. Mandatory Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Doug Joubert Thu, October 8, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tulane 2026 Football Schedule 6:30PM, 10/16 In a battle of colors Saturday morning in West Point, the Tulane Green Wave open the defense of their American Conference 2025 championship by visiting the Army Black Knights. Both teams enter the contest at 2-2 on the season. Team Schedules The Wave has lost its road contests against ACC defending champion Duke to open the season, then versus Big-12 opponent Kansas State two weeks later. Sandwiched between and after the two trips were home contests against Sun Belt teams, which Tulane claimed victories in both: South Alabama in the home opener and Southern Miss two weeks ago. The Green Wave had an open date last Saturday before its conference opener this weekend. Army opened the season at home with a 56-point shellacking of Bryant University out of the Coastal Athletic. The Black Knights followed with an American Conference loss at Michie Stadium versus South Florida, an early open date, then a league victory at Temple before falling at Louisiana Tech last weekend. See the PFF comparisons between Army and Tulane here. The Black Knights opened a 3.5-point favorite over the Green Wave earlier this week. That number has dropped to 3-point Army advantage since Monday. As of this writing, 81% of the money bet is on Army, giving the points to Tulane. Tulane Has Something to Prove: Our On SI Tulane Prognostication This 2026 version of Green Wave football has, if anything, been consistently inconsistent. Open the season with your new starting quarterback, who is replaced after 30-minutes, whose replacement is replaced a little over two-and-half games later, and whose replacement of the replacement is replaced for one play. Show an erratic rushing offense that can slash opponents with gigantic games from various running backs, but have nothing on a regular basis . Big passing plays to big players, but with drops and throws that sometimes don't come close, showing communication and concentration issues. Offensive and defensive fronts that are growing and progressing, but is their growth rate fast enough? Stop an opponent with three-and-outs on defense on consecutive drives, then have huge rushing gaps open in the defensive front seven or wide open receivers in the secondary. To have this much variety in results is confusing and awkward. There is plenty of talent on this team. With 60-returnees from the 2025 playoff team and some solid additions, think Jaylin Lucas, Fat Hill, Macho Stephenson, Ed Smith IV , this team should be hitting stride. But it's not. Instead, it is showing how consistently inconsistent it can be, which you cannot do against a team like Army. The Black Knights are the least penalized team in the American Conference only getting 16-flags on the season. They are the 5th least in all the NCAA. They do not make mistakes. If you are inconsistent, the discipline of Army will expose that, and expose it quickly. No matter how much coaches and players talk about defending the Black Knights option, it's another thing to actually do it. To defend it will take that word we keep on bringing up: consistency. We have not seen that from this Tulane team this year. They have to prove that they can be a team that does things well and does them on a regular basis. They have yet to do so. We think the big play will be open for Tulane, as the Black Knights give up more yards per play than any other team in the American, almost 7-yards a pop. If the Wave offensive front is able to open the holes for the running back and protect the quarterback, whoever that may be (we believe it should be Trace Johnson , but we've been wrong before), there will be big chunks available. However, we also believe Army's multiple option attack will be the undoing of the Green Wave defense. On SI Tulane Pick: Army 35 - Tulane 28 Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. This matchup puts Tulane’s athleticism against an Army offense capable of shortening games with sustained rushing possessions. Tulane Needs to Maximize Its Possessions Tulane enters this matchup after an uneven opening month, but the Green Wave have enough offensive capability to create problems for Army. The larger challenge is understanding that opportunities could be limited. Playing Army often means fewer possessions because of the Black Knights’ commitment to the ground game. That makes efficiency particularly important. Tulane can’t afford repeated three-and-outs or turnovers that allow Army to control another five or six minutes of clock. The Green Wave need to make their opportunities count and put the Black Knights in situations where they have to play from behind. Defensively, assignment discipline becomes the primary concern. Army’s offense doesn’t require explosive passing production to control a game. If Tulane consistently loses leverage or misses tackles at the line of scrimmage, the Black Knights can methodically dictate possession and keep the Green Wave offense on the sideline. The Black Knights responded with a 21-17 road victory at Temple, giving them a 2-1 record through their first three completed games. The offensive formula remains built around the ground game. Army can shorten a matchup by stringing together rushing first downs, which makes every opposing possession more valuable. That approach becomes even more effective at Michie Stadium if the Black Knights establish an early lead. Army has also been a dependable team against the spread recently, covering in four of its last six games with one push. The Black Knights don’t necessarily need to dominate statistically to put themselves in position to win. Their style naturally reduces variance and creates fourth-quarter games where one possession can decide the outcome. Tulane vs Army Picks and Predictions Pick: Army Against the Spread Army is my side in this matchup. Tulane has enough talent to win outright, but playing the Black Knights at Michie Stadium presents a difficult stylistic challenge. Army’s ability to control possession limits the number of opportunities Tulane gets to establish offensive rhythm, and the Black Knights have already shown they can survive close games. As long as the market remains around a field goal, I prefer Army at home. Pick: Under the Total The Under is my preferred total. Tulane has gone Under in seven of its last nine games, including four consecutive conference games, and Army’s offensive approach naturally consumes clock when it is working properly. The Green Wave’s best strategy also involves avoiding turnovers and preventing Army from gaining additional possessions. The recognition highlights the history, accomplishments and continued service of Army divisions as part of the Honored Division theme featured throughout the 2026 football season. The 7th Infantry Division represents Soldiers and units stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington. History of the 7th Infantry Division Known as the Bayonet Division, the 7th Infantry Division began its journey when it was first activated in December 1917 during the height of World War I. Elements of the division saw service during the Lorraine Campaign in 1918. The division was initially formed by combining Regular Army units stationed around the United States, ranging from Georgia, Texas and Oklahoma to Ohio and Vermont, while drawing its officers from the Regular Army and Officer Training Corps. Among its early commanders were two West Point graduates: Brig. Gen. Charles H. Barth, USMA Class of 1881, who assumed command in January 1918, and Maj. Gen. Edmund Wittenmyer, USMA Class of 1887, who took command in October. Following the Armistice on Nov. 11, 1918, the division served as an occupation force and conducted training in France before returning to the United States in 1919. The 7th Infantry Division was briefly posted at Fort Riley, Kansas, and Camp Meade, Maryland, before being inactivated in September 1921, as part of the post-World War I drawdown, although its 14th Infantry Brigade and various other elements remained on active duty. In July 1940, the division was reactivated at Camp Ord, California, under the command of Maj. Gen. Joseph W. Stilwell, a USMA Class of 1904 graduate. away.headline: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense
away.blurb: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense As they practiced on Tuesday for game prep coming off their bye week, Green Wave running back Jamauri McClure was a sight for sore eyes out there, participating in team drills without a non-contact jersey for the first time since he went down with a fractured foot in fall camp. This year's room looks a lot different in comparison. Maurice Turner is playing his best football right now. Jaylin Lucas has gotten some work out in space a bit more this week of prep. Johnnie Daniels has shown that he can throw a killer block as much as he can shoot through a gap. However, the return of McClure is what fans have been clamoring for since the news first got out that he was hurt. Now that he's had ample time to recover, his return should be a major boost for a Tulane offense looking to make the most out of and stretch out what should be expected to be limited possessions against the Army Black Knights Saturday. NFL Week 5 NFL picks vs. spread (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Maddy Hudak Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The best ability is often availability, and the Tulane Green Wave certainly have some good news on that front ahead of American conference play. But while head coach Will Hall told media members on Tuesday that he and the team feel that they're a better football team than when we last talked to and saw them last two weeks back, they have a lot to prove on the road to kick off their conference slate. An essential thing they're looking for is an identity on offense. Well, a lot of that can be solved by a strong rush attack that McClure instantaneously boosts. When McClure started taking over the starting running back job towards the end of the year last season, it was clear that he had a different gear and set of traits than what we were seeing from that room. Further good news on that front is that nothing appears to be up with Turner, who ended up limping a bit at the end of his 74-yard touchdown run against the Southern Miss Golden Eagles, as he also was practicing in full with no non-contact jersey. But the true finesse of that room lies with McClure. Another major returnee was wide receiver Zycarl Lewis, who got injured during the season opener against the Duke Blue Devils and hasn't practiced or played since. He was also not in a non-contact jersey on the practice field Tuesday. McClure averaged an impressive 6.5 yards per carry last season. The redshirt sophomore had eight total carries until Week 12 of last year against the FAU Owls. In the final five games of the season, he added 75 touches for 83 total carries for 540 yards and two touchdowns.

away.blurb: News Sports Life Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLLEGE Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane Ken McMillan Middletown Times Herald- Record Updated Oct. 6, 2026, 9:47 a.m. ET In the end, Army's 21-19 loss at Louisiana Tech on Saturday night was just a non-conference game and didn't affect the American Conference standings. However, the Black Knights are having trouble building on positives. "It's very hard to play perfect,'' said Monken, who also points out the margin for error is slim for his West Point teams. "We're going to strive to it.'' Monken pointed out that Army had too many missed assignments, played with poor fundamentals at times and didn't help themselves with six penalties, but he's not given up on the squad. A dominant win over Bryant in the opener, followed by a crushing late loss at home to South Florida. A tough road win over Temple, followed by a stumbling loss as a small favorite at Louisiana Tech , dropping the Black Knights to 2-2. "We're not going to let this game kind of derail our season,'' said senior center and co-captain Brady Small. "We're going to go back, we're going to watch some film, we're going to learn and get ready for Tulane, another conference game. So just use this as fuel to the fire to get us a win at home.'' Army is a three-point favorite over Tulane for Saturday's noon ET start. Army is 1-1 in American action, and needs a win vs. the Green Wave to stay in contact with the 1-0 leaders: Florida Atlantic (4-1 overall), Memphis (4-1), Texas San Antonio (4-1), Alabama Birmingham (3-2) and North Texas (3-2). Army will face FAU and Memphis but not the other three this season. "Honestly, we've just got to attack the adversity at hand,'' said back Samari Howard. "We can't let this be a lull in our preparation. Overall, we've got to come together as a collective and tackle the adversity and get ready for the next week and the week after that.'' "I don't believe anybody loses momentum unless they stop believing,'' head coach Jeff Monken said. "And I don't think our guys will stop believing. ... If we allow it to derail us, then shame on us. Weve got to learn from it, and each game is independent of the last one. I don't think we allowed last week (win over Temple) to linger into this week. We weren't patting ourselves on the back for such a great job.'' Monken always reminds people that winning college football games is hard. "I love our team,'' he said. "They're tough as nails. They compete, and we played all the way to the end tonight.'' West Point and New Orleans are separated by more than 1,300 miles, but the football programs at Army and Tulane remain very familiar. The Green Wave have a long history with the Black Knights, dating back to 1953 when the two schools battled to a scoreless draw. Next to service academy rivals Navy and Air Force, Army and Tulane have met quite often, 21 times since 1996. Tulane was a founding member of Conference USA in 199

picks.headline: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Texas Longhorns final score predictions: Red River Rivalry could see a familiar trend
picks.blurb: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Texas Longhorns final score predictions: Red River Rivalry could see a familiar trend - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Buccaneers-Cowboys updates Guardians-White Sox updates A'ja Wilson MVP — again NFL Week 5 NFL picks vs. spread Caitlin Clark on Fever future Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 8, 2026 at 4:46 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners will take on the Texas Longhorns in the Red River Rivalry, and it could be closer than some think. The Oklahoma Sooners and Texas Longhorns have one of the biggest rivalries in sports. The Red River Rivalry is truly a spectacle . But the last few years haven't been as much of a game as we, as sports fans, have hoped for. This one could be the same way. Texas is the No. 1 team in the country. Oklahoma is no longer ranked, and shouldn't be. But Texas seems beatable despite being No. 1 overall. They could have lost to Tennessee not long ago. Yet the Sooners, with their baggage, still have a chance this weekend. However, not many are picking them to win. Final score predictions for Oklahoma vs. Texas Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame: Texas 21, Oklahoma 10 This feels like an ugly, low-scoring battle for much of the afternoon, with both defenses dictating the pace. Oklahoma's defense presents a major challenge for Texas, forcing Arch Manning to make a couple of crucial plays in difficult situations. Manning doesn't need to put up huge numbers, but he delivers when the Longhorns need him most and does just enough to keep the offense moving. Oklahoma's bigger issue is its offense, which struggles to sustain drives against a talented Texas defense. The Sooners find a few opportunities but can't capitalize enough to keep pace. Texas eventually creates some separation late, with Manning making the key throws to secure a hard-fought 21-10 victory in a game that never feels particularly comfortable for either side. Craig Smith , A to Z Tennessee: Texas 26 Oklahoma 9 I've watched Oklahoma a number of times this season, and I haven't seen many Power Four offenses worse than the Sooners' this year. I also haven't seen many defenses better than the Longhorns' this year. Colin Simmons is one of college football's most dominant defenders, totaling 5.5 sacks against Tennessee in one of the best overall defensive performances we've seen from a player and a team this season. Now, a floundering OU offense with no answers for getting John Mateer and the passing attack going will have to find a spark against one of the country's best defenses. I don't expect it will go any better than it did for the Sooners against Georgia. OU gives Texas some short fields, and that's all the Horns need to take control. Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida: Texas 19, Oklahoma 7 We've seen some wild things in Red River, and this game likely won't be an exception. The one thing that stands out is Oklahoma's offense. I don't trust what John Mateer is going to be able to do. He's gone from a fun quarterback at Wazzu to a player with a broken brain. I don't think Mateer will do much against the Longhorns, but I can see the defense getting the Sooners on the board because that unit can flat-out play. Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama: Texas 27, Oklahoma 19 Typically, Red River is one of the more anticipated games on the college football schedule, but that doesn't seem to be the case this year. That has little to do with Texas, however, as the No. 1-ranked Longhorns have held up their end of the hype deal; it has everything to do with Oklahoma, OU's offense, and John Mateer. The year-two leap at Oklahoma hasn't come to fruition, and Mateer may have regressed from how he looked pre-thumb injury to his current state. But I don't think it's all on Mateer. Oklahoma just doesn't have easy buttons on offense outside of Isaiah Stategna, and Ben Arbuckle hasn't exactly inspired much confidence with his scheme. I don't see a world where OU can score enough to keep up with the Longhorns. Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma: Texas 19, Oklahoma 13 The Oklahoma Sooners are in a bad spot right now. As we write this, they're dismissing their freshman wide receivers. But in other news, the offense is broken. And there's really no fixing it. However, the defense is still good enough to win them games. They just need decent play from the offense from time to time. I still don't think that happens this week. They're not healthy. Meanwhile, Texas looks good, especially on defense. Their offense can be efficient but has its own issues. This one is going to go to the Longhorns once again. The Texas Longhorns and Oklahoma Sooners will meet in Dallas this weekend for a huge SEC showdown. Texas has won three of the last four games in this rivalry after losing four straight from 2018 to 2021. The Longhorns are having the better season, and they have the better roster, but the result of this game has been close in some years when it shouldn't have been. CBS Sports' Chris Hummer and Brad Crawford made their predictions for the game, and they have Texas winning. Hummer has the Longhorns winning 20-17. "Historically, this game is almost always close," wrote Hummer. "Nine of the last 14 regular-season matchups were decided by a possession or fewer. I haven't seen anything so far this year that makes me feel differently about this game. I have more faith in Texas than Oklahoma. … At the risk of far oversimplifying a complicated game, I feel very confident in saying the QB who plays best, be it Texas' Arch Manning or Oklahoma's John Mateer, will win this game. I have slightly more faith in Manning at this point, so give me the Longhorns to win in a close one." Crawford, meanwhile, has Texas winning 24-14. "I just can't envision a reality in which Oklahoma scores enough points with this offense against Will Muschamp to warrant picking the cover here," noted Crawford. "Even with an extra week to sort out the struggles with the passing game under John Mateer, this Oklahoma team plays with little confidence when it has the football, and that means something against the No. 1 team in the country, hoping to tee off on the quarterback." picks.headline: No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset
picks.blurb: No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation October 9, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football The Sooners head to Dallas with a struggling offense and stingy defense. Fresh off a bye week with a 4-0 record, the No. 1 Texas Longhorns head up I-35 for the annual Red River Rivalry against the Oklahoma Sooners, who have struggled thus far in 2026 — Oklahoma has a 2-2 record on the year and has failed to score more than 14 points in each of their last three contests. On paper, this is a matchup that should favor the Longhorns, but if history has shown anything, nothing matters once these two teams take the field at the Cotton Bowl. Scoring points against the Oklahoma defense is doable but will undoubtedly be the biggest challenge facing the Longhorns. “This is always a unique game because you can take record, stats, and all those things and throw them out the window,” Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. “You’ve got to play the game and you’ve got to play the game the right way.” The struggles for the Sooners start on the offensive end. Returning quarterback John Mateer has failed to effectively move the ball through the air and the running attack ranks 131st in the FBS in yards per game. Second-year offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle has made his money with Mateer at the helm, a partnership that is now in it’s fourth year and dates back to their time together at Washington State, but is currently testing the patience of Oklahoma fans given the offense’s lack of scoring. “Coach Venables, I know he’s probably sitting there thinking he wishes the record was a little bit different, but man, his teams play hard, and this team’s no different,” Sarkisian said. “They play hard. They’re an excellent defensive football team. They’ve got draft picks all over on the defense. Offensively, they’ve got playmaking ability similar to us. They’re trying to find their way to to find that level of consistency. But one thing I can be assured of — we’re going to get their best shot, and so I think it’s important for us that we focus on what we need to do so that we can play our best football.” With concerns across the Sooner offense, this year’s rendition will likely be determined by the success of the Longhorns finding the end zone in the Cotton Bowl. If the Longhorns can score points, things could get out of hand. Here’s what to expect on Saturday. As mentioned, the Oklahoma offense is headed by Arbuckle and Mateer. Arbuckle is a young and forward-thinking coordinator with a track record of quarterback development and roots in the Air Raid. At 31 years old, he has already helped develop Bailey Zappe, Austin Reed, and Cam Ward. His offense utilizes tempo and the run game to stretch defenses and create passing windows. With the athleticism of Mateer and the inability to create an impactful rushing attack otherwise, Arbuckle has adapted the offense to feature a quarterback run threat on nearly every play. Averaging just 22 points per game and coming off a bye week, a few new wrinkles are all but guaranteed from Arbuckle on Saturday. Much has been made of Mateer’s play at quarterback this season. The returning starter for the Sooners came into the season with lofty expectations after a turnover-prone 2025 season. Through four games, his play has been disappointing, prompting Venables to admit that he considered benching his starting quarterback at halftime of the Georgia loss. Mateer has completed 66.1 percent of his passes for 883 yards and eight touchdowns while adding 41 carries for 76 yards. However, Mateer has turned the ball over six times in four games, including three first-half turnovers last week against Georgia. Pro Football Focus has tracked eight throws by Mateer as turnover worthy this season. Holding on to the ball is priority number one for Mateer, who has looked rattled in the pocket the season. He’s missed reads, held on to the ball, and fired inaccurately on numerous occasions. Keeping Mateer uncomfortable sets the tone for the Texas defense. Nearly everything else is downstream of whether the Longhorn front can keep him guessing and rushed. Keeping Mateer’s legs out of the game will be another key for Texas — if Mateer can extend plays or effectively pick up first downs on designed runs, things get significantly more complicated for the Longhorn defense. Expect a heavy dose of quick, high-completion throws to start the game in order to neutralize the Texas pass rush and get Mateer into a rhythm. The lead back for the Sooners is junior Lloyd Avant. Avant is a 5’10, 212-pound ball carrier from Humble who has racked up 164 yards and a touchdown on 42 carries (3.9 YPC). A transfer from Colorado State, Avant was expected to compete for snaps with Tory Blaylock, but has been thrust into the starting role due to Blaylock’s hamstring injury. Against UTEP, Avant looked strong, rushing for 79 yards on 15 carries; however, in the three games since, he has carried the ball 27 times for just 85 yards. Blaylock came into the season as the leading back, but is recovering from injury. He’s gotten a handful of carries, but its clear that the coaching staff does have not believe he is close to 100 percent. With an additional week to recover, it’s very possible that he contributes in a more meaningful way on Saturday. Regardless of who takes handoffs, improvement is needed on the ground. After finishing 113th in rushing offense last season, the Sooners are 133rd in yards per rush and t-134th with two rushing touchdowns on the season. Despite an offseason of revamping the rushing attack, things have regressed through four games. “It’s frustrating because I feel like I’m not doing my part,” said tight end Rocky Beers , via OU Insider . “There’s always one miss here, one miss there, and it’s costing us... We’ve just got to believe in our blocks and hold onto them as long as we can.” Getting back to running the ball was undoubtedly a point of emphasis over the bye week and something that the Longhorns will need to thwart on Saturday. Wide receiver Perhaps the most talented player on the Sooner offense is leading wide receiver Isaiah Sategna. A transfer from Arkansas, Sategna leads the offense in receptions (20), yards (267), and longest play from scrimmage (53). His two touchdowns are tied for the most on the team. Listed at 5’10, Sategna isn’t a huge target but can be dangerous. His quickness can generate missed tackles and additional yardage after the catch, so closing in quickly will be important come Saturday. Sategna forced 22 missed tackles last season and half of his receiving yards this season have come after the catch. Transfers Trell Harris and Parker Livingstone were brought in to supplement Sategna but neither has been effective thus far. Harris remains sidelined with an injury and Livingstone hasn’t been able to make a difference, though this will undoubtedly be a big game for him after transferring from Texas during the offseason. Stopping Sategna will be the key to keeping the wide outs locked down, a task that Longhorns defensive coordinator Will Muschamp has to feel good about. Veteran tight end Rocky Beers, a Colorado State transfer, has proved to be a reliable weapon for Mateer in the passing game, tallying 18 catches for 255 yards and two touchdowns this season, which is the best on the team outside of Sategna. One of three tight ends brought in from the portal by new position coach Jason Witten, Beers has looked the part this season. His route running creates windows for Mateer and he has enough size to be a matchup problem on smaller defenders. When Oklahoma makes it to the red zone, Beers is a frequent target, something that Texas will need to take away come Saturday. Offensive line The running game has struggled for the Sooners and a big reason for that falls on the shoulders of the offensive line. This group has failed to keep a clean pocket, generate push, and open running lanes. If Oklahoma hopes to turn things around offensively, the five up front will need to step up their performance, immediately. Against Georgia, the Oklahoma offensive line switched things up, sitting Eddy Pierre-Louis at guard in favor of Heath Ozaeta and Noah Best, but it made little difference. E’Marion Harris, the right tackle, still looked a step slow while star left tackle Michael Fasusi remains sidelined with a shoulder injury. I’d expect this group to get additional help in blocking from tight ends and running backs, as well as a heavy dose of plays designed to get the ball out of Mateer’s hand quickly. This group has yet to show anything special through four games, increasing pressure on longtime position coach Bill Bedenbaugh, whose tenure dates to the Bob Stoops era. The Oklahoma offense has sputtered to start the year. Poor quarterback play coupled with a lack of rushing attack and porous offensive line has resulted in little points being scored. With a bye week to prepare for the Longhorns, I’d expect a sharpened game plan out of the gate that features quick passes and unique ways to get the ball out of Mateer’s hands. For the Longhorn defense to find success, getting pressure is key. When Mateer feels the pass rush, he has shown an inability to make good reads and deliver accurate passes. Keeping him from feeling comfortable will be a point of emphasis for the Longhorns. Outside of Mateer, limiting Sategna and Beers is the next priority. Forcing someone besides these three players to make a difference should spell success for the Longhorns. For every concern about the offense, the defense boasts a strength. This unit has been salty thanks to a solid crop of returners despite a mediocre offense on the other side of the ball that can’t finish drives and turns the ball over. Moving the ball through the air against the Sooners has been particularly tough. Allowing 122.5 passing yards per game, the OU secondary ranks fourth in the country, and is led by returning producers that understand the scheme and have the physical talent to implement it successfully. Opponents convert 23.1 percent of third downs, the third best in the entire country, meaning staying ahead of the chains will be essential for the Texas offense. The best method to attack this defense has been via the run. Averaging 115.5 yards per game on the ground and 3.23 yards per carry, this aspect remains in the top third of the country but lags behind the stellar pass and third-down defense. Don’t be mistaken by the record or score against Georgia — the Oklahoma defense can get after it. Defensive line Up front, there are four players that Texas will need to handle — defensive ends Taylor Wein and Adepoju Adebawore, and tackles David Stone and Jayden Jackson. In the middle, Stone and Jackson are a formidable duo. Stone was one of the Sooners’ most highly-regarded returners after notching 43 tackles a year ago. Now in his third year at Oklahoma, the 6’3, 312-pound lineman will be looking for his first win in Dallas. Next to him, Jackson is quite the player. Last season, he tallied 28 tackles and 3.0 sacks, including being honored as the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week for his performance against Auburn. This duo up front has been a big reason why the defense has been stout thus far. Wein lines up on the outside and had a breakout campaign last year after somewhat surprisingly winning the starting role. He takes over as the ma

As of today, it has been 1,094 days since OU reached the end zone, dating back to the Sooners' 2023 upset (fluke) win over the Horns. However, even as Texas has held Oklahoma to just three field goals over the last two Red River Rivalries, the Longhorns haven't exactly put on offensive showcases . This year, the expectations for the offenses aren't all that different, and the oddsmakers have the 2026 Red River Rivalry as low-scoring as the last couple of seasons. But don't worry, they still have the Horns coming out on top. Early odds for No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma in Red River Rivalry Spread: -7.5 Texas, +7.5 Oklahoma Moneyline: -330 Texas, +260 Oklahoma Over/Under: +/-39.5 points While the oddsmakers have Texas walking away with a victory by more than a touchdown, they also have the point total set below 40 points between the two teams. In other words, they expect the final score to be somewhere around 23-16 or 24-16, seemingly alluding to the idea that the Sooners will be able to find the end zone in the Cotton Bowl, a first in nearly 1,100 days by the time the game kicks off on Saturday. The moneyline favors Texas a little more heavily, with someone having to bet $330 on the Horns just to profit $100, but only having to wager $100 on Oklahoma to walk away with a $260 profit. Meanwhile, in Oklahoma's only Power Conference games (losses to the then-unranked Michigan Wolverines and No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs), the Sooners have only averaged 11.5 points per game, and most of that is coming from the defense or special teams. Texas and Oklahoma are scheduled to kick off at 2:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Oct. 10, and the game will be broadcast on ABC. By James Parks | October 7, 2026 One of college football’s great rivalry games renews this weekend as the Red River Shootout finds No. 1 ranked Texas facing off against Oklahoma in a critical test for both sides, if for very different reasons just a month into the 2026 season. Texas, still the class of the SEC , owns signature wins against Ohio State and Tennessee that catapulted it into the top AP ranking. Oklahoma fell out of the poll after falling to 2-2 and is once again facing structural questions around what remains a very anemic offense. What do the analytics department think of this week’s matchup? For that, let’s turn to the SP+ college football model to project the outcome, and use it to lock in our own prediction. Texas vs. Oklahoma score prediction: Can Arch Beat the Sooners' Defense? Sep 26, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates after a college football game between Tennessee and Texas at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn. on Sept. 26, 2026. Mandatory Credit: Brianna Paciorka-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) It may not come as a surprise that the Longhorns are getting the favorite treatment against the Sooners, and by a decent margin, too. SP+ predicts that Texas will defeat Oklahoma by a projected score of 27 to 17 and will win the game by an expected margin of 9.9 points in the process. The model gives the Longhorns a very strong 73 percent chance of victory, one of the biggest discrepancies of any game this weekend. SP+ is a “tempo- and opponent-adjusted measure of college football efficiency” that attempts to predict game outcomes by measuring “the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football.” How good is it this season? So far, the SP+ college football prediction model is 146-122-3 in its picks against the spread with a 54.4 win percentage. What actually happens? Can the Longhorns defend their No. 1 ranking? Sep 4, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) in action during the game against the UTEP Miners at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images That’s a different question. Even with a Texas win, its place atop the AP poll could be in danger anyway as pollsters may be more impressed with what happens between No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama as they face off in primetime. A big win over the Sooners could sway enough voters to stay at No. 1 , and everything looks like it should go the Longhorns’ way. Even with questions around Arch Manning’s continued development at the quarterback position. Sure, Texas is 4-0 and Manning looks much better than this time last year, but he has also clearly still not performed to expectations, either. Arch is a decent 63 percent passer but is making some curious decisions and doesn’t look completely at ease in the pocket against better-quality fronts. Against an Oklahoma defense that, despite everything, remains one of college football’s best – 4th against the pass, top 25 in scoring, and 3rd in third-down conversions – Manning could get seriously rattled early. But the Longhorns still have an advantage of their own on defense. They have battery of elite pass rushers who can wreck OU’s blockers, shrink the pocket, and get at John Mateer on a regular basis. That should give the Texas offense enough chances to separate and pull away late. Horns by 10. What happens? Texas beats Oklahoma, and covers the spread. However, what should come as no surprise is that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had another idea in mind : no update. With star players like running back Hollywood Smothers, tight end Nick Townsend, and defensive lineman Justus Terry all missing time this season, Longhorn Nation has been eager to see their guys back in action. Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see what we should expect on Saturday. "I think we're healthier than we were a week ago at this time," Sarkisian said in his game preview press conference, continuing his refusal to share injury updates beyond what he puts in the SEC-mandated availability reports.
