Based on the final injury list from Texas's game against Tennessee, one could easily assume that Smothers will be good to go against the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend as the Horns prepare for the annual Red River Rivalry. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. Offensive lineman Braydon Nelson was listed as probable on the report. That lines up with what Morris said on Tuesday, which was that he expected Nelson to be available for Saturday's game. The Cowboys went so far as to list him on the depth chart at both left tackle and right tackle with Ashton Lepo and Shaun Torgeson. Morris did say that he expects Lepo and Torgeson to start. The 3-1 Ducks are already dealing with a thin margin for error as they prepare to host a 4-0 UCLA team that profiles as a potential dark-horse contender under first-year coach Bob Chesney. Both are coming off bye weeks following Week 4 wins, each impressive for different reasons. Oregon took down USC 41-27 on the road and showed an explosive offensive gear, even after losing starting quarterback Dante Moore to a scary injury in the first half. UCLA turned heads by traveling cross-country for a 54-3 win over Maryland , marked by an all-systems dominance which suggested the Bruins are no joke. While Chesney's first season since arriving from James Madison is off to a perfect start, this marks a new kind of challenge. The Bruins have not played a team currently ranked in the top 60 of the CBS Sports 138 and will be up against Oregon, which entered the season at No. 2 in the AP poll. After a stunning Week 2 loss at Oklahoma State , the Ducks began living up to preseason expectations in their Week 4 win over the Trojans. Oregon vs. UCLA: Need to know Dante Moore unlikely to play: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore returned to practice this week after suffering a concussion on a late hit in the first half of the Ducks' Week 4 win at USC. However, he's unlikely to play against UCLA. That should mean another opportunity for Dylan Raiola . The Nebraska transfer completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC and looked comfortable leading a talented Ducks offense. Having such a solid second option should reduce any urgency Oregon might feel to get Moore back on the field. Raiola is a former two-year starter for the Cornhuskers and a five-star prospect who is one of the nation's most talented second-string quarterbacks. UCLA's rushing attack : UCLA ranks No. 4 nationally in rushing offense at 281.5 yards per game on the ground. James Madison transfer Wayne Knight is the name to know. The 5-foot-7 speedster is tied for third nationally with nine rushing touchdowns. He reached the 100-yard mark in each of the Bruins' first two Big Ten games. Oregon is familiar with his game after he ran for 110 yards on 17 carries in the Ducks' 51-34 victory over James Madison in last year's College Football Playoff quarterfinal. The difference this time is that Knight has a better supporting cast around him. CFP implications: Oregon's Week 2 loss at Oklahoma State put the Ducks' postseason aspirations in early jeopardy. After UCLA, the only ranked opponent left on Oregon's schedule is Ohio State (Nov. 7). While having a manageable slate is helpful in some respects, there's also no guarantee the Ducks would make the CFP as an at-large team with two losses if there wasn't much meat on their resume. CBS Sports' College Football Forecaster projects Oregon with a 51.1% chance to make the 12-team field with a win over UCLA. That drops to 19.6% with a loss. UCLA would have a 33.3% chance to reach the CFP if it beats Oregon and an 8.3% chance with a loss. What happens if the ground game hits a wall and the Bruins fall behind on the road against a team with superior talent? They have not demonstrated the passing chops required to erase a deficit, especially not against a team of Oregon's caliber. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks UCLA vs. Oregon Winner With Dante Moore's Status Unclear Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy picked Oregon to beat unbeaten No. 21 UCLA on Saturday at Autzen Stadium, betting that the Ducks' run defense can contain first-year coach Bob Chesney's ground game whether Dante Moore or Dylan Raiola starts at quarterback. McElroy took the Ducks 31-21 on his Always College Football podcast and built the pick around a red-zone trend for Oregon coach Dan Lanning. "Dan Lanning is 39-1 in his career when Oregon gets more red-zone trips than the opponent," McElroy said. Who starts at quarterback for Oregon? Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola throws a pass as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Raiola replaced Moore at the Coliseum and went 19 of 25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns. However, McElroy pointed to the Nebraska transfer's history against ranked teams. "If you look back at his time at Nebraska, he was 0-5 against ranked football teams," McElroy said. "Well, UCLA is ranked." A Raiola start would also come one week before Oregon faces Nebraska. Wayne Knight vs. Oregon run defense UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) looks on after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Running back Wayne Knight, who followed Chesney from James Madison , has 445 yards and nine touchdowns on 49 carries against FBS opponents. McElroy noted the Bruins average 7 yards per carry, the best mark in the country. But Oregon has allowed just nine runs of 10 or more yards. The Bruins' passing game is the concern. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava has thrown four touchdown passes, which McElroy said ranks 118th nationally, and Chesney's teams struggle when they have to lean on the pass. "Bob Chesney is 20-1 as an FBS head coach when his team runs fewer than 30 pass plays," McElroy said. "He is 1-3 when they have to throw it 40 or more times." Why did McElroy pick Oregon? Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning runs out to the field with players before a game against the Portland State Vikings | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. "Oregon will completely sell out against the run," McElroy said. "So once the Bruins are forced to throw the ball, that's when the matchup starts to tilt pretty hard in the direction of the Ducks," McElroy added. UCLA's best upset path runs through turnovers. The Bruins are plus-8 in turnover margin, tied for third nationally, while Oregon has given the ball away twice all season. UCLA also averages 10 penalties per game, which McElroy said ranks 137th out of 138 teams, and that number becomes harder to overcome in a road environment like Autzen. History favors the Ducks, too. Oregon has won the last five meetings, and McElroy noted UCLA's last win in Eugene came in 2004, when Lanning was a freshman linebacker at William Jewell. picks.blurb: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Buccaneers-Cowboys updates Guardians-White Sox updates A'ja Wilson MVP — again NFL Week 5 NFL picks vs. spread Caitlin Clark on Fever future Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in the midst of a much-needed bye week, enjoying some time off after a strenuous and pressure-filled first month of the 2026 season. Through four games, we've seen the Ducks start at No. 2 in the AP poll, drop to No. 6 after an underwhelming win over Boise State before losing to Oklahoma State, dropping them all the way down to No. 21. They then took care of Portland State, 84-0, moving them up a spot before a pivotal road matchup in Los Angeles with USC . The Ducks never blinked, even when quarterback Dante Moore had to leave the game via ambulance with a head injury, as backup Dylan Raiola and some timely defensive plays powered Oregon over USC, 41-27. It was as impressive of a win as we've seen from the Ducks over the past two seasons, and one that they badly needed in order to keep their goals of winning a national championship alive. Now, Oregon gets to take a breath and relax with a Week 5 bye. But that's not all that the players and staff are doing, as they'll be getting a jumpstart on preparing for the upstart UCLA Bruins , who will come to town in Week 6. We'll follow suit, providing an early deep-dive preview of how the Bruins ' season has gone so far, a breakdown of the offense, defense, special teams and players to watch with game and betting details to boot. Let's start with UCLA's resume, as they head into the matchup with Oregon looking to continue their undefeated season. UCLA's Resume Through Five Weeks Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins wide receiver Aidan Mizell (1) dances in the end zone with wide receiver Landon Ellis (11) and wide receiver Semaj Morgan (4) after catching an 83-yard touchdown reception in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Week 1: W 45-24 @ Cal Week 2: W 28-10 vs. San Diego State Week 3: W 52-38 vs. Purdue Week 4: W 52-3 @ Maryland The Bruins got off to an impressive start in the newly-hired Bob Chesney era, taking down the Tosh Lupoi-led Golden Bears on the road after a dominant second half. Chesney, who commanded James Madison to the College Football Playoff a year ago, relied upon several of his former Dukes that followed him to Westwood in the season-opener. The start of the season was strong, and so was last game for UCLA. The Bruins went into Maryland and stomped all over the Terrapins, picking off four passes and racking up 475 total yards. The early, 10:30 PT start didn't hold them back, as they jumped out to a 20-3 lead at halftime and only added to the lead after the break. Sandwiched between those two spectacular outings were victories over San Diego State and Purdue, with the offense carrying them in the former and offense in the latter, showing how well-rounded the Bruins are in 2026. Offensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins running back Jaivian Thomas (21) celebrates with offensive line Hall Schmidt (65) after scoring a touchdown in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images While last season was discombobulated at times for the Bruins offensively, new coordinator Dean Kennedy — coming over with Chesney from James Madison — has brought a revitalized, intelligent and, thus far, highly-successful offense to UCLA. Kennedy has a history of elevating previously subpar offensive units, as he developed quarterback Kyle Trask at Florida, turned Holy Cross into the Patriot League scoring leader and orchestrated the ninth-ranked scoring offense at James Madison in 2025. Now, he's doing the same thing at UCLA with a spread-based system that emphasizes physicality and explosiveness at the point of attack. Kennedy's units have consistently been among the best at creating explosive plays, both on the ground and through the air. While the Bruins won't go under center much at all, instead standing in the shotgun or pistol, they aren't afraid to run it right down the defense's throat. Through the air, the route combinations aren't necessarily complex, but they make it easy on the quarterback to read with a progression-based system. Defensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Trent Hendrick (25) celebrates after intercepting a pass in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Also brought over from James Madison, Colin Hitschler is the defensive coordinator for the Bruins with a goal of instilling an uncommon physicality that hasn't been seen in Westwood for some time. And thus far this fall, UCLA has, for the most part, lived up those goals. The Bruins mostly operate out of a 4-2-5 defensive alignment, following the trend of opting to put an extra defensive back on the field over a lumbering linebacker. But make no mistake, the linebackers have plenty of talent to handle the middle of the field themselves, with a pair of seniors coming in at first and second on the team in tackles through four games. Hitschler isn't afraid to send pressure, having loads of success against Maryland in forcing the quarterback to make decisions under duress that turned into four interceptions. Expect more of the same come Week 6, with Hitschler putting the onus on the offensive line to protect whoever trots out at quarterback for the Ducks. Special Teams Breakdown Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA kicker Mateen Bhaghani (15) kicks a field-goal during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images The Bruins have modest special teams units, with average kickoff and punt return marks with the same for the coverage units — though the return aspect could change in a blink with a pair of return men with elite speed waiting back there. In the kicking game, kicker Mateen Bhaghani has been solid in converting 4-of-5 field goals and all 23 extra points. It's his third season as the starter at UCLA, and he's made 82.8% of his field goals with a long of 57 yards — a massive advantage at the college level. Punter Curtis Gerrand also has a big leg, averaging 45.7 yards per punt on 15 boots thus far. Players to Watch Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) passes in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images There's an abundance of talent across the roster, yet these three players will have to be accounted for by the Ducks if they're to get their fourth win. QB Nico Iamaleava 2026 Season Stats: 62-for-99, 820 yards, 4 TDs, 2 INTs / / 35 rushes, 143 yards, 1 TD Analysis: Iamaleava hasn't quite needed to show off his world-class athleticism this year, with his backfield mate stealing much of the thunder in the first month of the season. That's not to say the former Tennessee starter can't scoot, as he's run for 1,077 yards and 11 touchdowns in four seasons while tossing 38 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. Not the most refined passer, Iamaleava — like many college quarterbacks — feasts on short and long throws, but hasn't quite developed the intermediate aspect of his game. Still very talented, Iamaleava is commanding mid-to-late round draft buzz, though he does have one more season of eligibility remaining. RB Wayne Knight 2026 Season Stats: 49 rushes, 445 yards, 9 TDs / / 8 catches, 88 yards Analysis: Yes, you read that right. Wayne has nine touchdowns four games into the year, with six coming in the first two games. Standing just 5-foot-7 and 193 pounds, Knight makes up for his lack of size with elite speed, vision and playmaking ability. At James Madison in 2025, Knight broke off runs of 73, 59, 58 and 49 yards with 57 and 49-yard gains on receptions. Always an ability to hit a home-run, the Ducks will have to be cognizant not to lose Knight behind the Bruins' offensive line. LB Sammy Omosigho 2026 Season Stats: 37 tackles, 3 sacks, 4 forced fumbles Analysis: Though the Bruins added 2025 Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year Trent Hendricks to the roster recently, he's still getting acclimated so we'll spotlight Sammy Omosigho here. The 6-foot-2, 239-pound four-year Oklahoma transfer has gotten off to a fast start at UCLA, leading the team in tackles and recording three sacks from his linebacker spot. Hitschler sends the former Sooner quite often on pressures and he makes plays as evidenced by his four forced fumbles in four games. picks.blurb: my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores SPORTS & TEAMS PERSONALITIES POPULAR SEARCHES College Football Can UCLA Upset Oregon On The Road? Who Wins Red River? Klatt's Week 6 CFB Picks Updated Oct. 8, 2026 11:34 a.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Headlining Week 6 of the college football season is a top-10 matchup in Georgia vs. Alabama, and the annual Red River Rivalry between Texas and Oklahoma. The Crimson Tide and the Bulldogs split last year when Alabama took down Georgia in the regular season, but the Bulldogs answered right back with an SEC title win over Bama. Texas remains atop the 2026 rankings with a comfortable 5-0 record that includes top-15 victories over Ohio State and Tennessee, and the Sooners look to hold off the Longhorns with a rebound win after a big loss to Georgia. Notably, UCLA and Bob Chesney will travel north to Eugene to face Oregon, where Chesney fell to the Ducks as JMU's head coach in the College Football Playoff last season. With a dominant run game and a shaky Oregon defense, the Bruins have a chance to hand the Ducks their second loss of the season. Here are FOX Sports' Joel Klatt's Week 6 picks and previews: Georgia 27, Alabama 24 Spread: Alabama 1.5 Moneyline: Alabama -122, Georgia +102 Klatt's thoughts: "This one is going to be an amazing game. Kirby Smart always has a great defense. They are great, once again. They have the No. 1 defense in the country as it relates to yards per play. They can get after it. They're going to have to get after it because Alabama's offense is explosive. Alabama can play offense, and Keelon Russell can throw the ball down the field. I think NFL evaluators should be salivating when he becomes available in the NFL Draft. He reminds me a lot of the way Michael Penix Jr. played at Washington for Kalen DeBoer, and yet he's more explosive and more mobile as a runner. So it's a deadly combination. "I think that Georgia has to put pressure on them. If they don't put pressure on Keelon Russell, I think Georgia loses the game. They've got to impact him somehow … it will be about the Georgia defense. I know the offense will be methodical. They will try to stay on schedule, they've got a quarterback who plays great in the fourth quarter … I think the worse the weather, the better for Kirby and Georgia. I don't know if Alabama can run the football without the impact of a great passing game. "I'm going to take Georgia … who I think is the best team in the country." Klatt's straight-up pick: Georgia Klatt's pick against the spread: Georgia +1.5 Texas 20, Oklahoma 10 Will Arch Manning succeed against Oklahoma's defense? (Photo by The University of Texas Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Spread: Texas -7.5 Moneyline: Texas -325, Oklahoma +260 Klatt's thoughts: "Texas and Oklahoma. Texas has won three of the last four meetings with Oklahoma. Texas is No. 1 in the country right now. They should be ranked No. 1. They are better on paper than they are on film. They've been wildly inconsistent as a team and specifically on the offensive side. I don't have a lot of worries about the Texas defense. The offense has not been very good … Penalties, not throwing the ball well, Arch has not played very well … they've got the best résumé, two top-15 wins. They've earned this position where they're at. Now they play a top-five defense in OU. "OU can play defense now. Their issue is definitely not their defense. In a lot of ways, these teams mirror each other. What if I told you Oklahoma is 112th in yards per play offense? They turned the ball over, they couldn't do anything against Michigan. What if I told you that Texas is 108th in yards per play offense? They're basically the same team … they've got great defenses and great offenses that are woefully underperforming. So what do I see in this game? I think it's low scoring. Just to give you some context, by the way … Texas is behind Colorado and Michigan in yards per play offense. When I tell you that they're better on paper than on film, it is the truth. "I think Texas wins, and covers, in a low-scoring affair 20-10, Texas and Arch Manning get the win at Red River." Klatt's straight-up pick: Texas Klatt's pick against the spread: Texas -7.5 Oregon 45, UCLA 32 The last time Bob Chesney was in Oregon, he was coaching JMU in the College Football Playoff. (Photo by CFP/Getty Images) Spread: Oregon -11.5 Moneyline: Oregon -455, UCLA +35 Klatt's thoughts: "Bob Chesney has UCLA undefeated right now. They're looking to pull off a huge upset in Eugene. Oregon is going to have to do a lot better at stopping the run than they have done during the course of the season. UCLA can absolutely run the football. They have one of the best run games in the country, averaging seven yards per rush. And they feature a guy in Wayne Knight that is explosive. Now here's the thing with UCLA: their quarterback can also run. He might not be the most dynamic runner, but Nico Iamaleava can absolutely threaten you in the run game. If I'm an Oregon fan, that makes me very nervous because of what Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker did, running that game in Stillwater. Wayne Knight is outstanding. "By the way, Bob Chesney took his JMU team to Eugene for the College Football Playoff, and yes, Oregon won handily, but guess what? JMU scored over 30 points … I think that [UCLA is] going to score some points here. Now the question will become, can Oregon match them and exceed them on the opposite side? I expect to see [Dylan] Raiola, he has bit of a penalty for turnovers, even though we didn't see that at USC when he came off the bench, but if you look back at his time with Nebraska, there are some turnovers there … I don't quite trust the UCLA defense. This is a defense that allowed 38 points to Purdue. "Oregon gets it done. I think Oregon wins 45-32, and they cover the 11.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Oregon Klatt's pick against the spread: Oregon -11.5 USC 32, Penn State 14 The Matt Campbell era is not off to a great start, and Joel Klatt doesn't think it's going to get better this week. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Spread: Penn State -1.5 Moneyline: Penn State -122, USC +105 Klatt's thoughts: "USC on the road, going east. USC, now 5-1, is at Penn State, who's now 3-2 and is unranked, and the bottom has kind of fallen out for Matt Campbell … What is going on? Penn State is favored by 1.5. [USC] just played awful football for six quarters. … The big question for me is, is USC going to beat themselves, or will they play a cleaner game? … When you just evaluate the teams and the product on the field, by 1.5 seems wild. USC is facing their old defensive coordinator, with a familiar piece there in D'Anton Lynn. I think the familiarity favors Lincoln Riley … USC should be able to run the ball. Penn State can't tackle anybody. The only one that gets in the way for USC, in my estimation, are the costly mistakes. Those might show up. I don't think USC's defense is great, but I think they're better than people give them credit for. "Penn State can't do anything on offense. They really miss their wide receiver, Koby Howard. He was averaging 100 yards per game on nearly 30 per catch. Since he went down, they've really struggled on offense. Rocco Becht has struggled on offense. They couldn't do anything against Northwestern. Couldn't do anything in the second half against Wisconsin. USC is better than Wisconsin and Northwestern talent wise. Klatt's straight-up pick: USC Klatt's pick against the spread: USC +1.5 LSU 28, Kentucky 10 Will Stein has Kentucky exceeding expectations in his first year at the helm, but LSU's defense looms. (Photo by Zach Del Bello/Getty Images) Spread: LSU -9.5 Moneyline: LSU -345, Kentucky +275 Klatt's thoughts: "LSU at Kentucky. LSU is favored by 9.5. Kentucky beat a very average Texas A&M and a very average-to-bad South Carolina team. They hung with Alabama for a half and then kind of got ran out of that building. I still am a bit concerned for LSU about the health of their quarterback. Sam Leavitt can't play the way that he normally plays ... his health is paramount for this team. Their defense is outstanding. This is where I think it really makes a huge difference in this game. Their defense is better than Alabama's defense. Kenny Minchey is going to see guys who can get after the passer. Princewill Umanmielen has eight sacks … Will Stein is doing awesome … he's exceeding expectations for Kentucky . But LSU is a different animal. This defense is a different animal. They can rush the passer and run everywhere. They're one of the best defenses in America. "I think Kentucky has to play their best. Do I anticipate them playing their best after the emotional win a week ago? No. History suggests that over the course of the season that very rarely can teams do something on the positive side, in an emotional fashion, and back it up with consistency the next week. So, I don't see Kentucky playing at the level they need to stay within the 9.5. "I got LSU winning this game 28-10. LSU covers the 9.5." away.headline: Oregon Ducks Injury Report Delivers Dante Moore News Before UCLA
away.blurb: Coming out of a bye week with extra time to rest and recover, fans waited for the first injury report for the No. 13 Oregon Ducks' matchup against the No. 21 UCLA Bruins with perhaps more anticipation than usual. Below are the players listed as out, doubtful, questionable and probable. The Big Ten requires each program to update its availability beginning three days ahead of the game. Oregon's next injury report is expected at 5 pm. PT on Thursday. While fans will have to wait a little longer to see him in action, Moore's teammates expressed the boost in morale the team gained from seeing him in practice. Lanning addressed having him out there during his Wednesday press conference. "Yeah, I think the biggest thing is just being able to see a smile on his face to get around and be around his teammates and his brothers and do that at a high level, which is fun," Lanning said. "Everybody has a smile on their face getting to see Dante out there with us this week, and it's been fun seeing him compete." "He had an expectation when he stepped out there on the field and performed at a really high level, and everybody had confidence in him because they see him do it a lot in practice," Lanning said. "You get a lot of reps in practice, regardless of where you're sitting." As soon as Moore announced in the offseason that he'd forgo the 2026 NFL Draft and return to Oregon, the outside expectation from many was that the transfer Raiola would back up Moore and become a regular starter in 2027. But with Moore's injury and slow build-up to his return to play keeping him out against the Bruins, Saturday could mark Raiola's starting debut at Oregon. Ducks linebacker Jerry Mixon expressed on Tuesday that Raiola's prior experience and his preparation give the team confidence in him. "He's been ready the whole time, learning from Dante," Mixon said. "Yeah, he's been starting for two years, so he knows what to do when he get out there." away.headline: Will Oregon QB Dante Moore play against UCLA? See the injury report
away.blurb: Moore, who suffered a concussion and had to be taken off the field in an ambulance in the first half of the Ducks ' Sept. 26 game against USC, was officially listed as "out" on Oregon's Big Ten-mandated availability report that was released Wednesday. Wide receivers Jeremiah McClellan and Jack Ressler, offensive lineman Trent Ferguson, inside linebacker Brayden Platt, and running back Simeon Price were also listed as out. Oregon's secondary depth also could be thin on Saturday as starting safety Aaron Flowers and reserve cornerback Aaron Scott Jr. were both listed as doubtful. picks.headline: LSU vs. Kentucky game predictions: Can LSU and Lane Kiffin stay on track, or will Kentucky continue their hot start under Will Stein?
picks.blurb: LSU vs. Kentucky game predictions: Can LSU and Lane Kiffin stay on track, or will Kentucky continue their hot start under Will Stein? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Buccaneers-Cowboys updates Guardians-White Sox updates A'ja Wilson MVP — again NFL Week 5 NFL picks vs. spread Caitlin Clark on Fever future Petre Thomas-Imagn Images; Jordan Prather-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 8, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tigers and Wildcats should be a fun one in the Bluegrass State on Saturday night. Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers head to Lexington this weekend for a showdown with Will Stein's Kentucky Wildcats. LSU has bounced back from a deflating loss at Ole Miss by throttling Texas A&M and McNeese State in Baton Rouge. Meanwhile Kentucky comes in after clipping South Carolina 35-34 in overtime last weekend in Columbia. Which of these 4-1 teams will stay in the thick of the SEC and playoff hunt midway through the season? Our college football writers weighed in with their score predictions. Kentucky 25, LSU 24 The LSU Tigers have been good this season, but we know the history of Lane Kiffin. He has a tendency to lose a game he shouldn't, and it seems to happen at least once per season. This is the kind of game that fits the bill. Will Stein has done a fantastic job with the WIldcats. He's got them playing hard and they are very well coached. This has trap game written all over it. Tyler Forness , A to Z Sports Florida LSU 32, Kentucky 31 This is another game where LSU falls behind early, just as they did in Oxford, as Kentucky rides an electric early energy from a wild Kroger Field crowd to an early double-digit lead. But the Tigers' talent on both sides of the ball eventually recovers from an early gut punch and storms back. The Tigers' defense starts to get home and forces a mistake from Kenny Minchey that swings the tide. Sam Leavitt delivers a last second score to break Kentucky hearts and give LSU a win that could look quite good at the end of the season. Craig Smith , A to Z Sports Tennessee LSU 33, Kentucky 21 This is a sneaky good SEC matchup to watch this week between LSU and Kentucky. LSU can't go into this game underestimating this 4-1 Wildcats team, or they'll be leaving Lexington 4-2 with a tough road ahead to making the College Football Playoff. The key for LSU will be limiting mistakes on offense because I believe their top-three defense in yards allowed per game will get the job done against Will Stein's offense. On the flip side, the Wildcats are going to have their hands full defensively with what is a balanced LSU offense. Quarterback Sam Leavitt and running back Dilin Jones will both have big days on offense for LSU, and the Tigers will show up on the road with a double-digit win in SEC play. Brandon Little , A to Z Sports Ohio State Kentucky 31, LSU 28 Kentucky continues its surprising run under head coach Will Stein, with quarterback Kenny Minchey keeping his hot streak alive against LSU. Minchey makes enough big-time throws to keep the Wildcats within striking distance throughout the afternoon, but it's his ability to make plays with his legs that ultimately becomes the difference. A few key scrambles extend drives and keep Kentucky's offense on the field when it matters most. LSU has plenty of offensive success of its own, with Sam Leavitt making several impressive plays and keeping the Tigers in a back-and-forth battle. But late in the game, Leavitt makes one mistake too many, throwing a backbreaking interception that gives Kentucky the opportunity it needs. The Wildcats capitalize and hang on for a thrilling 31-28 victory. Ryan Roberts , A to Z Sports Notre Dame LSU 30, Kentucky 20 Kentucky has quietly been one of the better stories in college football this season as first-year head coach Will Stein has proven himself right thus far. The Wildcats gave Alabama hell in the first half, beat the Texas A&M Aggies, and just knocked off South Carolina in overtime. They may not have the firepower to keep up with LSU, but I wouldn't be shocked if they kept it close. Part of that is because LSU has been banged up to start the season, with multiple pass catchers and even QB Sam Leavitt dealing with injuries. In all, I don't think the Tigers get put on upset alert, but I expect the Wildcats to put forth a good effort. The LSU Tigers will look to avoid a "letdown" this weekend in a road matchup against the Kentucky Wildcats. Saturday will mark the first matchup between the two programs since 2021 when Kentucky beat LSU 42-21 in Lexington. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of LSU vs Kentucky ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, made his predictions on Tuesday for this weekend's biggest games, and he has LSU just barely getting by Kentucky. "I'm taking the LSU Tigers to win the game 30-24," said McElroy . "I think they're going to win this game with the pass rush, and I do think there's going to be plenty of opportunities for LSU's defensive front to create some advantages behind the line of scrimmage. "But with (LSU QB) Sam Leavitt still a little bit limited right now, I think this one has a chance to stay pretty close for a really long time. Kentucky's comeback last week (against South Carolina) was historic, but against this pass rush, they can't afford to be playing from behind from start to finish." It's never easy to win on the road in the SEC. Kentucky isn't as daunting of a venue as some other places in the conference, but it can still be a challenge. LSU would love to win this game by multiple touchdowns, and maybe they do, but just simply getting the win is the top objective for the Tigers on Saturday night in Lexington. picks.headline: LSU defense preview: Kentucky offense has to stay on schedule
picks.blurb: LSU defense preview: Kentucky offense has to stay on schedule - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Buccaneers-Cowboys updates Guardians-White Sox updates A'ja Wilson MVP — again NFL Week 5 NFL picks vs. spread Caitlin Clark on Fever future Story by Wildcats Wire LSU defense preview: Kentucky offense has to stay on schedule Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:53 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football hosts a top ten team in the LSU Tigers under the lights of Kroger Field, and the bluegrass is as fired up as ever coming off the largest comeback road win in program history. The energy is at an all time high in Lexington, as Will Stein has kicked off his first year as head coach with a 4-1 record. Kentucky was dropped out of the AP top 25 after their road win at South Carolina, this will add some motivation as this is just the third time since 2000 a team was dropped from the top 25 following a win. We previewed Lane Kiffin's dynamic offense he is bringing with him, now it is time to preview the Tigers defense that is statistically one of the best in the conference. Defensive coordinator Blake Baker was retained by Kiffin as he has done a phenomenal job with the Tigers defense. This is a defense loaded with talent, but will unfortunately be without the leader and green dot in Whit Weeks. LSU gave up 32 points on the road at Ole Miss, they have allowed just 44 total points in their other four games combined. That game was big for a lot of reasons, but when you look at the statistics per secstatcat.com; Kentucky and Ole Miss have very similar numbers offensively. Kentucky - SEC Rank Ole Miss - SEC Rank Early Down Conv. % Ole Miss, similar to Kentucky, has also struggled on converting 3rd downs this season. Ole Miss has definitely been better on third downs, but is still an area they need to improve on. Both Kentucky and Ole Miss have canceled out their third down woes by converting on early downs. They are first and second in the SEC in converting on early downs, and they join Georgia and Alabama as the only SEC teams that are converting over 50% on early downs. This is an area Kentucky has to continue to have success in to win this game, staying on schedule is a huge factor in this football game. Kentucky cannot get in 3rd and long as that is when LSU can overwhelm you with the talent they have on the defensive line. Princewill Umanmielen followed Kiffin over from Ole Miss and he is a true game wrecker off the edge. Umanmielen leads all of college football with eight sacks on the season, this will be a true test for both tackles Lance Heard and Malachi Wood. Another interesting aspect of this matchup is the relationship of Kentucky offensive coordinator Joe Sloan and LSU defensive coordinator Blake Baker. They worked together for years at Louisiana Tech and obviously spent the last couple of season together at LSU. They know each other really well, and they could know tendencies of each other as play callers that could create advantages in certain situations. Sloan knows a good amount of the roster at LSU, and it is intriguing to see if that can pose advantages for the Wildcats. The LSU defense has been incredible against the pass game, as they lead the SEC in EPA/dropback allowed. Their secondary is led by corner DJ Pickett and safety Ty Benefield, both players are NFL Draft prospects that can make plays at every level of the field. Their starting slot corner Dashawn Spears tore his ACL and is out for the season. This has led Ty Benefield to playing that spot in nickel formations, and he will have his hands full with Louisiana native, breakout true freshman slot receiver Kenny Darby This will be an extra special game for a lot of people on Kentucky's offense. Offensive coordinator Joe Sloan was fired as offensive coordinator at LSU before making the move to Lexington. Kenny Darby broke high school receiving records in the state of Louisiana and was committed to LSU for a long time. Wide receiver Nic Anderson also transferred over from LSU. Kentucky's offense will continue to be difficult for opposing defenses, as the scheme just constantly forces you to communicate. This LSU defense has a ton of playmakers, but Kentucky can find success as long as they stay on schedule. Kentucky is one of the best offenses in creating yards before contact and the offensive line has been steady in pass protection all season. The Wildcats offensive line has to find a way to win the line of scrimmage in this game, and it is easier said than done with this stout LSU defensive line. Kentucky will have to find success on offense to win this football game. Expect Lane Kiffin and Charlie Weis to put points on the board as they always do. This is a defense similar to Alabama, where Kentucky struggled to consistently move the football on in week two. There is no doubt the Wildcats offense has improved since then, but we will see just how much they have improved on Saturday. There weren't any surprises as five Tigers were listed as out with no players showing up as questionable or doubtful. Trey'Dez Green, Whit Weeks, DaShawn Spears, Phillip Wright III, and Charles Ross II were the five designated as out. Spears, Wright, and Ross are out for the season, while Green and Weeks are expected to miss all of October, with a chance to return in November. Few SEC teams have dealt with the volume of significant injuries LSU has in 2026. Spears was a difference-maker at the STAR position -- he's out for the year. Green and Weeks were All-SEC caliber players at their respective positions, and LSU will miss them for at least a month. On offense, with Green out, LSU will rely on more four-receiver sets. When LSU needs a tight end on the field, Zach Grace will get most of the reps. LSU is also trying to get Roman Mothershed involved as a pass-catching tight end. At linebacker, LSU will rely on Davhon Keys to fill in for Weeks. TJ Dottery will slide into Weeks' role and wear the green dot, with Keys taking on Dottery's position. away.headline: Updating LSU football's offensive depth chart after injuries, lineup moves
away.blurb: The biggest shift was the loss of star tight end Trey'Dez Green. Green suffered a knee injury in Week 3 and has missed LSU's last two games. Green is expected to miss all of October, with a chance to return in November. Phillip Wright III (OUT, season) This is the position where LSU has suffered the biggest loss, with Trey'Dez Green out for a significant period. In Green's place, Oregon transfer Zach Grace has gotten most of the reps. LSU moved wide receiver Roman Mothershed to TE to get another receiving threat at the position. Mothershed scored his first touchdown in an LSU uniform in the win over McNeese. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are 4-1, just about where we expected them to be at this point. LSU's lineup looks a little different than it did in Week 1. Injuries, along with typical early-season shuffling, have adjusted the Tigers' depth chart, especially on offense. Up front, the offensive line has stayed mostly the same, but there's been some tinkering at left guard. At running back, Dilin Jones remains RB1, but there's been some movement down the depth chart. Let's take a look at LSU football's updated offensive depth chart through five weeks. No surprises at quarterback. Sam Leavitt remains LSU's QB1. It's clear that Landen Clark won the QB2 job and USC transfer Husan Longstreet is LSU's QB3. Wisconsin transfer Dilin Jones is LSU's feature back. He earned the job in the spring and hasn't looked back. Down the depth chart, though, the lineup isn't as consistent. Stacy Gage was LSU's RB2 to start the season, but that role belongs to Harlem Berry now, who rose from RB4 in recent weeks. Eugene Wilson, Jackson Harris, and Winston Watkins have emerged as LSU's top-three wide receivers, though Watkins is coming off a rough game where he dropped two touchdowns. Jayce Brown and Tre Brown both produced at their previous stops, but haven't seen much action with the first-team in recent weeks. home.headline: LSU football injury report | Who made the list ahead of Kentucky game?
home.blurb: News Sports Business Living Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals LSU LSU football injury report | Who made the list ahead of Kentucky game? Cory Diaz Lafayette Daily Advertiser Updated Oct. 7, 2026, 7:29 p.m. CT BATON ROUGE — LSU football' s initial injury report for this weekend's game at Kentucky is out. For the first time this season, there are no surprises on the report for Lane Kiffin and the Tigers (4-1, 1-1 SEC). LSU does not have any players listed as probable, questionable or doubtful on the report released Wednesday, Oct. 7 by the SEC. Weeks and Green have not been ruled out for the rest of the season but have suffered leg injuries that will keep them out for a substantial amount of time. The No. 10-ranked Tigers face No. 25 Kentucky (4-1, 1-1) inside Kroger Field on Saturday, Oct. 10 (6 p.m. CT, ESPN). As expected, star linebacker Whit Weeks, tight end Trey'Dez Green , safety Dashawn Spears, as well as reserves and special teams players Charles Ross II and receiver Phillip Wright Jr., are on the list. Spears, Ross and Wright have suffered season-ending injuries. Weeks fractured his fibula against Texas A&M on Sept. 26 and has had a successful surgery to correct it. Green sprained his knee in the Ole Miss game and has missed the past two games for LSU. But earlier this week, Kiffin said the tight end was getting closer to playing. home.headline: Cal GM Ron Rivera on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele Injury vs. UNLV: It Was `Avoidable'
home.blurb: The Bears (2-3, 1-1 ACC) return home Saturday to face Virginia Tech (3-2, 1-1) in a 12:30 p.m. kickoff at Memorial Stadium. Will JKS miss his first game in two seasons or could he return to face the Hokies? We don’t know. Turns out Sagapolutele continued to show “some symptoms” during the second half and he now is among four Cal players undergoing multiple tests every day as part of the Bears’ concussion protocol program. Safety Kingston Lopa is also facing those protocols, Lupoi said. Besides Lopa going out with the head injury, the Bears played portions of the UNLV game without defensive backs Cam Sidney and Daniel Harris, both ejected after targeting penalties. Cal GM Ron Rivera on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele Injury vs. UNLV: It Was `Avoidable' Skip to main content SI.COM Quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele is among 10 Cal starters dealing with injuries — one of four in concussion protocol — coach Tosh Lupoi reported Tuesday. Cal is not required to provide details about injuries, although we will get status updates when the ACC releases its initial player availability chart on Wednesday night. We do know this much: Cal football athletic director and general manager Ron Rivera was not happy with the play that led to Sagapolutele leaving the game in the final minute of the half at UNLV. Rivera called the injury “avoidable.” Cal was trailing 24-7 when JKS rolled right and threw incomplete on first-and-10 from his own 25-yard line. UNLV linebacker Elias Rudolph, a transfer from Miami, flung Sagapolute to the artificial turf and the sophomore QB’s head bounced off the artificial turf. No flag was thrown, but Rivera clearly believed that should have happened. “JKS’s concussion, in my opinion, was avoidable. And I agree with Tosh, something should have happened,” he said. “When the quarterback throws the ball and the defender sees him throw the ball, there’s no reason to allow him to violently grab a guy and swirl around him and throw him to the ground. "Just go back and watch the tape. That’s all I’m going to say about that.” Lupoi removed Sagapolutele from the game after watching him stagger back to the huddle. At halftime, he was told JKS was cleared to play, but Lupoi said he didn’t feel comfortable sending him back onto the field. With backup Jackson Brousseau performing well at quarterback, Cal rallied to take a 25-24 lead in the second half before the Rebels answered to win 39-31. The closest Lupoi came to providing a hint as to whether Sagapolutele might face Virginia Tech was when he offered, “He was cleared to go back in at one point. That tells you it was a minor whatever-you-want-to-call-it.” Cal already has been playing without injured running backs Adam Mohammed and Carter Vargas. The Bears were desperate enough at the position that wide receivers Tyree Sams and Carson Perry-Smith were given snaps — and carries — at running back in Saturday. “You may or may not see that this week,” Lupoi said. home.blurb: Cal was without quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele for the entire second half after he left the game in the final minute of the second quarter when he hit his head hard on the turf. He reportedly was cleared to return but Cal opted not put him back in the game with a head injury. Cal safety Kingston Lopa left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter and did not return. Bears starting nickel back Cam Sidney was ejected from the game for targeting in the first quarter. Cal defensive back Daniel Harris was ejected for targeting in the fourth quarter. INDIVIDUAL STAT OF THE GAME II: Cal limited all-Mountain West running back Jai'Den "Jet" Thomas to 46 yards on 16 carries. This game was considered a tipping point for Cal’s season, and it tipped the wrong way. Cal’s second straight loss reduces Cal’s chances to finish the season with a winning record for the second straight season. Before the season began, a 4-1 Cal record after five games seemed possible and a 5-0 start was not out of the question. A 2-3 mark at this stage was not what Cal supporters had in mind. The Bears have little momentum heading into the heart of its ACC schedule, which starts next Saturday with a home game against Virginia Tech. The outside complaints from Cal fans will continue, and the Bears are on the verge of becoming irrelevant this season. Cal rallied from a 24-7 halftime deficit to take the lead, but ultimately the Bears lost to UNLV 39-31 on Saturday afternoon at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Jackson Brousseau was the Bears' quarterback in the second half. Cal played the game without injured running back Adam Mohammed, the team’s leading rusher with 336 yards. RECORDS: CAL (2-3, 1-1 ACC), UNLV (3-2, 1-0 Mountain West) UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold. Although he passed for just 158 yards, he threw touchdown passes of 70, 36 and 10 yards and ran for a 55-yard touchdown. He also had a key 42-yard run and finished with 110 rushing yards. With Cal leading 25-24, UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold ran 42 yards to the Cal 12-yard line, which led to Arnold's 10-yard touchdown pass for a 32-25 UNLV lead with 9:38 left. KEY PLAY 1: On a fourth-and-2 play from the UNLV 47-yard line, Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed a pass to Tyree Sams, but it was a half-yard short of a first down. It turned the ball over the UNLV with 12:20 left in the first quarter with the game scoreless. KEY PLAY 2: Cal safety Kingston Lopa, who leads the nation in interceptions with five, left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter. KEY PLAY 3: Sagapolutele completed a 91-yard touchdown pass to freshman tight end Taimane Purcell, who covered most of the ground himself. It gave Cal a 7-0 lead with 11:30 remaining in the first quarter. KEY PLAY 4 : Cal starting safety Cam Sidney was ejected for targeting with 11:25 left in the first quarter. KEY PLAY 5: On a third-and-8 play from the UNLV 30-yard line, Rebels quarterback Jackson Arnold completed a 70-yard touchdown

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings CBS Sports experts Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer reveal their final picks for college football's best games of Week 6, highlighted by an epic SEC clash Getty Images There are a couple of teams with considerable College Football Playoff résumé-strengthening opportunities this weekend, none bigger than a pair of nationally ranked matchups pitting title contenders from the SEC and Big Ten. Second-ranked Georgia 's trip to No. 6 Alabama should bring high drama between two unbeatens, along with No. 13 Oregon 's tussle at home with No. 21 UCLA , two squads trying to claw their way closer to Ohio State and Indiana at the top of the Big Ten hierarchy. Sorting through the contenders, potential upsets and matchups that look considerably trickier than the betting lines suggest is exciting this time of year. We've already seen how quickly September confidence can disappear at some programs. Season results : Brad Crawford (35-8 straight up, 25-17-1 ATS), Chris Hummer (35-8 straight up, 21–21-1 ATS) Y'all, it's time to celebrate Hummer moving back to .500 on the season ATS after a 6-4 week. We both took wins with Alabama's cruise at Mississippi State and North Carolina 's easy cover against Notre Dame during a rain-soaked game in Chapel Hill. Picking Miami to cover was shaky for two-and-a-half quarters before the Hurricanes laid it on the Tigers down the stretch to stay unbeaten. I whiffed on Michigan -5.5 at Minnesota . Kyle Whittingham has so much to fix in Year 1 with the Wolverines. All odds via FanDuel . No. 20 Iowa (+3.5) at Washington Hummer ( Iowa +3.5) : These are two of the better defenses in the Big Ten. Both Iowa and Washington are top 31 units nationally, and those defenses have carried both teams early. This game will be decided by which offense can manufacture the most points. Usually, I'd feel good about Washington doing so. After all, the Huskies have Demond Williams Jr . at QB. But he's really struggled this season and is turning the ball over far too often. Meanwhile, Iowa actually ranks ahead of Washington in yards per play (6.24 vs. 6.04). Iowa is the better team. It might actually have more playmakers. But I do think there's value with a Huskies cover, even at 3.5 points. … Iowa 21, Washington 20. Crawford (Iowa +3.5) : This is never an ideal situation as a ranked road underdog on a Friday night against a team coming off an emotional performance. The market's telling us something here. Washington quarterback Demond Williams Jr. will be the best player on the field, but I'm trusting the Hawkeyes' defense in this spot to fare better than it did last time out against Heisman favorite and my pick to win the award, Jeremiah Smith . Iowa can maintain its spot in the national rankings and march toward a potential 11-1 finish with a win, but I don't think there are going to be enough big plays to pull it out. ... Washington 23, Iowa 20. No. 7 Indiana (-9.5) at Nebraska Hummer ( Nebraska +9.5) : Once again, Nebraska is off to a hot start. And once again, it has a chance to change the program's narrative against a ranked Indiana team. Were the Huskers to pull the upset, it'd be their first win over an AP Top 25 team since 2016! And I do think there's value with the Huskers in this one. Would I like 10 points instead of 9.5? Absolutely. But the Huskers have looked good enough up front to hang with Indiana. And while the Hoosiers have still been largely dominant, they've shown some cracks in the trenches and at QB, where Josh Hoover has been good but a tad inconsistent. I'm not calling for an outright upset, but I do expect this game to be close. … Indiana 31, Nebraska 27. Crawford (Indiana -9.5) : Matt Rhule's last win over a ranked opponent came at Temple on Dec. 3, 2016, when his Owls beat Navy . Nebraska has lost nine such matchups under his watch and is staring at No. 10 this weekend against the Hoosiers. Both of these teams like to run the football, and they're doing it aggressively this fall, but Indiana's the more seasoned group in spotlight games -- and that matters here. For me, this comes down to trust, and the unbeaten Huskers need to show me they're capable of punching up a few weight classes before I'm ready to bet on them. Indiana covers in Lincoln in a game that should have the Hoosiers' full attention. ... Indiana 31, Nebraska 17. Texas A&M at No. 14 Missouri (-3.5) Hummer ( Missouri -3.5) : Texas A&M got a much-needed Arkansas boost of confidence a week ago. But I still have major concerns about the Aggies. Missouri's been an elite rush defense this season, which is bad news for A&M's run game, which has struggled. And if Missouri is taking away the run, it will be on Marcel Reed to make up for that. And based on what we've seen so far this season -- Reed ranks 77th nationally in QBR -- I don't have a lot of faith that he'll win that matchup. Throw in an A&M secondary that busts far too often, and I think the Tigers match up well in this one. … Missouri 27, Texas A&M 21. Crawford (Missouri -3.5) : The Tigers have looked focused all season, and they're two stops in the fourth quarter at Mississippi State away from being unbeaten and potentially ranked inside the top 10. Austin Simmons hasn't thrown an interception yet, and Jamal Roberts is running with steam in the backfield without Ahmad Hardy to assist. Missouri grabs everyone's attention with its destruction of Florida , while Texas A&M is simply trying to put together consecutive competitive performances in the SEC. I would've made this one closer to a touchdown, so there's value here. ... Missouri 34, Texas A&M 24. No. 1 Texas (-9.5) vs. Oklahoma Hummer ( Oklahoma +9.5) : The results in this game have been surprisingly volatile the last four years, with a trio of Texas blowouts in that stretch. But historically, this game is almost always close. Nine of the last 14 regular-season matchups were decided by a possession or fewer. I haven't seen anything so far this year that makes me feel differently about this game. I have more faith in Texas than Oklahoma. But both offenses have struggled, with Texas ranked 108th nationally in yards per play and Oklahoma 112th. At the risk of far oversimplifying a complicated game, I feel very confident in saying the QB who plays best, be it Texas' Arch Manning or Oklahoma's John Mateer , will win this game. I have slightly more faith in Manning at this point, so give me the Longhorns to win in a close one. … Texas 20, Oklahoma 17. Crawford (Texas -9.5) : This might not be the prettiest rivalry game in Dallas if you like big plays, but I just can't envision a reality in which Oklahoma scores enough points with this offense against Will Muschamp to warrant picking the cover here. Even with an extra week to sort out the struggles with the passing game under John Mateer, this Oklahoma team plays with little confidence when it has the football, and that means something against the No. 1 team in the country, hoping to tee off on the quarterback. The Sooners score on special teams for one of their two touchdowns. .. Texas 24, Oklahoma 14. No. 21 UCLA at No. 13 Oregon (-11.5) Hummer (Oregon -11.5) : This is the first big test for UCLA and Bob Chesney. Oregon has far better talent, and it'll be up to the staff to bridge that gap. Chesney is at least familiar with Oregon, having faced them a year ago at James Madison . Where I worry about UCLA's ability to hold up in this one is up front. The Bruins rank 91st nationally in pressure rate allowed in pass situations, while Oregon, despite a slow start, still has one of the nation's best defensive lines. And even if Dante Moore doesn't play, I'm confident Oregon's offense will move the football with Dylan Raiola . Give me the Ducks to make a statement after their bye week. … Oregon 38, UCLA 24. Crawford (UCLA +11.5) : Games with conference championship and CFP implications are here to stay the rest of the way for those inside the national rankings now that we're nearing the midseason point. The Bruins haven't lost yet under first-year coach Bob Chesney, but they're still flying under the radar nationally, and they prefer it that way. Dante Moore returned to practice Monday for the Ducks and could play this weekend. Oddsmakers are truly undervaluing UCLA here. And I think if this game were in Los Angeles, we're closer to a touchdown or so spread. ... Oregon 30, UCLA 24. No. 10 LSU (-10.5) at Kentucky Hummer ( LSU -10.5) : There's some interconnectivity with this game. Kentucky offensive coordinator Joe Sloan was LSU's play-caller a season ago, and several former Tigers players or signees came with him. This matchup will come down to a few key areas. First, can Kentucky's receivers make enough plays? Notre Dame quarterback transfer Kenny Minchey has been good this

Georgia vs Alabama Prediction: Odds, expert picks, team and player news, betting trends, and stats
picks.blurb: Georgia vs Alabama Prediction: Odds, expert picks, team and player news, betting trends, and stats - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Buccaneers-Cowboys updates Guardians-White Sox updates A'ja Wilson MVP — again NFL Week 5 NFL picks vs. spread Caitlin Clark on Fever future Vaughn Dalzell Wed, October 7, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The two highest scoring teams in the country are the #6 Alabama Crimson Tide (5-0) and #2 Georgia Bulldogs (5-0); and lucky for us, they play Saturday night in primetime! Georgia is fresh off a smackdown on Vanderbilt, 38-14, while Alabama dismantled Mississippi State 56-23. This has game of the year potential, and there's been a lot of them in the SEC already! Georgia has the No. 1 rated offense and defense per PFF, averages the most points in the country, and allow the third-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) — and all of that will be put to the test against Alabama. The Bulldogs pitched a second-half shutout against Vanderbilt and won 38-14 after leading 21-14 at the half. Georgia has allowed 20 or fewer points in all five games and 44 points over the last three games against Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Vanderbilt. The offense put up 471 total yards of offense, doubled Vanderbilt's first downs (26-13), and held the Commodores to 85 rushing yards. Alabama is coming off arguably their most impressive performance of the season. The Tide destroyed Mississippi State, 56-23, never trailing in the game. Alabama outgained Mississippi State in yards 483-302, went 6-of-9 on third downs, and forced four turnovers (2 INT, 2 Fumbles). Keelon Russell had another dominant outing with 301 total yards and four touchdowns (3 pass, 1 rush). Russell is climbing the Heisman Trophy rankings and a win over Georgia would likely jolt him to the top spot. Alabama has owned the series against Georgia winning 10 of the past 12, but the Bulldogs won the previous matchup 28-7. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Georgia vs Alabama Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Time: 7:30 PM Eastern Site: Bryant-Denny Stadium City: Tuscaloosa, AL TV/Streaming: ABC Game Odds for Georgia vs Alabama The latest odds as of Tuesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Georgia Bulldogs (+102), Alabama Crimson Tide (-122) Spread: Alabama -1.5 (-112) Total: 52.5 points #2 Georgia Bulldogs Head Coach: Kirby Smart 2026 Record: 5-0 (3-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 51.4 PPG (1st) Defensive Points Per Game: 13.4 (12th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 97th 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 20th The Georgia Bulldogs Offense: Georgia is the highest scoring offense in the country which is odd because in years past, Kirby Smart has taken is foot off the gas against early season opponents. Georgia's scored 45, 41, and 38 points against SEC opponents so far with 471, 464, and 306 total yards of offense. Georgia ranks sixth in third-down offense (54.9%), fifth in passing efficiency (188.72), and 13th in turnover margin per game (+1.2). One area that will be of interest is Georgia's red zone offense is 51st in the country with a 25-of-28 conversion rate (89.3%), but the fourth-most red zone attempts. Georgia has to be aggressive in the red zone at Alabama. Field goals likely won't cut it. Georgia Player to Watch on Offense: QB Gunner Stockton In last year's SEC Championship Game, Gunner Stockton threw for three touchdowns on 20-of-26 for 156 yards. Georgia cruised 28-7. This matchup won't be as easy and could feature double the points. Stockton tossed three touchdowns versus Vanderbilt last week after combing for two touchdowns in the two weeks prior. Stockton hasn't been asked to do much this season due to all the talent around him, including the running back committee. Stockton has a 13:1 TD to INT ratio this season and a 75.7 completion percentage. The Georgia Bulldogs Defense: Georgia's allowing 244.6 yards per game (7th) and that will likely go up after this showdown. We know Georgia is great at getting pressure (PFF rank of 22 for pressure) or getting coverage sacks (PFF rank of 3 for coverage), but the two areas that will determine the game is third downs and red zone defense. Georgia's defense has a 33.8% third-down defense (44th) and have only allowed 11 red zone trips this season, but 10 of them have resulted in points (8 TDs, 2 FGs). Georgia Player to Watch on Defense: LB Chris Cole Chris Cole is a projected first round pick in the upcoming draft as a three-year player for Georgia. Cole opened the season with a half-sack, and added anther against Oklahoma with two fumble recoveries. Cole had 60 tackles last season, ranking fourth, and a team-leading 4.5 sacks. Cole has 22 tackles and 1.5 sacks to this season. Last year, Cole had five tackles versus Alabama and a sack. Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. #6 Alabama Crimson Tide Head Coach: Kalen DeBoer 2026 Record: 5-0 (3-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 49.6 (2nd) Defensive Points Per Game: 20.8 (51st) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 23rd 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 11th The Alabama Crimson Tide Offense: Anyone that says Alabama owns the best offense in the country is not a liar; they probably are. Alabama Player to Watch on Offense: QB Keelon Russell Keelon Russell now has a rushing touchdown in three-straight games and four out five, plus three or more passing touchdowns in three consecutive games. He is on fire and now the third in odds for the Heisman. Russell now has 11 passing touchdowns to two interceptions, 1,414 yards through the air, and 184 on the ground. Russell had his fewest pass attempts (22) on the season against Mississippi State but was efficient with a 72.7 completion percentage, 285 passing yards, and four total touchdowns. Georgia will be his toughest test yet, but if this is a shootout and Alabama wins, then Russell will be the favorite for the Heisman and Bama could climb as high as No. 1 or 2 in the AP Poll. The Alabama Crimson Defense: The Alabama defense may be flying under the radar this year because of how well the offense has been playing. The Tide allow 78.6 rushing yards per game (10th) due to teams falling behind and abandoning the run, rank 15th in third-down defense (27.5%), and have the seventh-best turnover margin per game (+1.4). "This game always seems to matter," Pollack said on the matchup on his podcast, "See Ball Get Ball." He thinks the winner of the game will advance to play in the SEC championship. Pollack describes Alabama as the country's "most improved team from the start of the season to where we're at now" in the season. The Crimson Tide are led by quarterback Keelon Russell and have the nation's No. 2 scoring offense. Pollack thinks that the weather is the only thing that "could ruin" the Georgia-Alabama game. Pollack predicts that Georgia is going to go on the road and win 31-28 at Alabama. "I think that I am going to trust Kirby (Smart) and the defense to make life harder on Russell than he's had it yet," Pollack said. "I think he is going to look more like a freshman than he has... I'm going to go Georgia." Pollack thinks Russell will continue to improve. Pollack went on the heavily praise Russell as "the next guy" that has been elite at Alabama. Pollack notes that the Alabama offense is explosive and leans on the big play, while Georgia is more focused on staying ahead of the chains and running the ball. "Bama can score at any point," Pollack said. However, it is Georgia who has the No. 1 scoring offense in the country. The Bulldogs have not trailed all season. Pollack notes that Russell has struggled at times (later noting that struggle is relative) against the blitz and that Georgia is blitzing more often than it has in the past. "Georgia is going to blitz. They're going to be aggressive," Pollack continued. He thinks that Georgia has to be able to get Russell on the ground and that will determine who wins the game. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 19 USC desperately needs a win to remain in the CFP hunt, while Penn State looks to avoid a 0-3 start in the Big Ten Imagn Images It's a must-have for both teams, as No. 19 USC hits the road to take on Penn State Saturday night in Happy Valley. Penn State enters the game with its season seemingly spiraling out of control. After a 3-0 start in nonconference play under new coach Matt Campbell, the Nittany Lions have dropped their first two Big Ten games, and didn't look particularly inspiring in either. The offense struggled mightily in losses to Wisconsin and Northwestern , and last week, the defense was gashed by Northwestern's rushing attack. Suddenly, a schedule that was considered one of the easiest in the Big Ten before the season began looks far more difficult for the Nittany Lions. Not that things have been much easier for their opponents. The Trojans are 5-1 on the season and are coming off a win, but have looked shaky for three straight games. They found themselves in a shootout with Rutgers three weeks ago, followed that up with a 14-point home loss to Oregon , and last week flirted with disaster against a Washington team that hadn't looked impressive to start the season. Now they're on the road against a team with its back against the wall, and a second loss (with Ohio State and Indiana still to come) could crush USC's playoff chances. USC vs. Penn State: Need to know It's the White-Out game: Penn State's White-Out game is a newer tradition in college football , having begun in 2007, but it's quickly become one of the games Penn State fans look forward to most. Everybody in Beaver Stadium is dressed in white and screaming at their absolute loudest. Unfortunately, the results haven't always matched the intensity. Penn State is only 11-7 in White-Out games, but that's partly because the Nittany Lions reserve the tradition for their toughest games. It's a battle of the two winningest QBs in college football: That fact probably caught you by surprise, didn't it? Well, it's true. Penn State's Rocco Becht comes into this game with 29 wins as a starting QB in his college career. That's more than any other QB in the country. USC's Jayden Maiava is tied for second with 24. So Becht will either widen the gap this week, or Maiava will narrow it. Penn State hoping to avoid a 0-3 start in Big Ten again: Last season, the Nittany Lions started 0-6 in Big Ten play. It was an unexpected slide that led to James Franklin's mid-season firing. If they lose here, they'll be 0-3 in the Big Ten for the second straight season. The last time that happened was the 2003 and 2004 seasons. Of course, Matt Campbell could take some solace if his team loses. He'd be the first Penn State full-time head coach to start his tenure with a 3-3 mark since Joe Paterno in 1966. I don't like either side of the total, so I'm being asked to back a Penn State team that's looked terrible lately as a favorite, or take a USC team that's really struggled on the road under Lincoln Riley as a small dog. Frankly, there's no right option here, and I don't recommend taking any side. But, unlike you, I don't have a choice, so I guess I'm less terrified of USC +1.5 than anything else. Becht has struggled in each of the past two games, leading to the losses for the Nittany Lions. While the struggles from Penn State aren't all on his shoulders, Becht does make a big difference to this team. For the season, the veteran signal-caller has thrown for 1,108 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Against an opportunistic Trojans defense, Becht will need to limit his turnovers, keeping the ball with the offense. USC has a strong offensive-attack, and if they are given more opportunities or shirt fields, it may be a tough game for Penn State. Penn State has the means to pull off an upset win against the Trojans in this game, and if they can, they could build momentum for the rest of the season. Penn State is having its annual White Out night and as someone who attended the game last year versus Oregon, I’m expecting a great game once again. USC is fresh off a 25-21 win versus Washington, which came down to the wire whereas Penn State was manhandled by Northwestern, 34-13. Penn State lost to Wisconsin (24-20) and Northwestern (34-13) allowing the most points of the season back-to-back weeks. Rocco Becht also threw interceptions back-to-back weeks and his first multi-interception game at Northwestern. The Nittany Lions are in danger of falling to .500 on the season and have a road trip to Michigan following USC. Matt Campbell is straying to feel the heat and will rely on his defense to dig him out of this hole. PFF ranks Penn State’s defense sixth in the country overall, but they’ve given up 861 yards in the last two games. Penn State has forced four turnovers in that span but turned the ball over four times as well. Turnovers could be the storyline of the 2026 White Out. USC bounced back after the loss to Oregon with a close four-point win over Washington. The Huskies converted two fourth downs on their final drive before failing on 4th and 10 with a shot to the end zone. The Trojans defense had its best defensive effort against a P4 opponent this team with 198 yards allowed to Washington ‘s quarterback Demond Williams Jr. and held the Huskies to a 1-of-12 mark on third downs. Jayden Maiava had the fewest yards (245) and touchdowns (1) on the season versus Washington. Maiava was only sacked once, but you better believe Penn State will be bringing the pressure at home. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us.
